items.title: Gombe awards seven road contracts covering 97km
items.description: …Projects to open up rural communities, boost economic activities in four LGAs By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Government has signed contract agreements with construction companies for the execution of seven road projects covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas. The projects, which span Balanga, Kaltungo, Shongom and Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Areas, are aimed at improving rural connectivity, facilitating the transportation of agricultural produce, enhancing access to markets and stimulating economic activities. The contract agreements were signed at a ceremony organised by the Ministry of Works and Infrastructure, attended by government officials and representatives of the construction companies. Speaking at the ceremony, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Hon. Shehu Yerima Abdullahi, said the projects were part of the infrastructure development agenda of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s administration to connect underserved communities and promote socioeconomic growth. He said the road projects demonstrated the government’s commitment to extending infrastructure development beyond urban centres and improving the living conditions of rural residents. Abdullahi charged the contractors to justify the confidence reposed in them by adhering strictly to approved engineering specifications, quality standards and contractual obligations. He stressed that timely completion and quality workmanship were non-negotiable, adding that the ministry would sustain monitoring and supervision to ensure the projects were delivered within the agreed timelines and required standards. Earlier, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Danladi Adamu, said the contract-signing exercise was an important step towards ensuring effective implementation, supervision and delivery of the projects. In their separate remarks, the Branch Manager of EEC International Limited, Mr Dong Jian; representative of the Managing Director of SWAS GRADE Limited, Engr. Christina Daniel; and Managing Director of DATUM Construction Nigeria Limited, Engr. Daher Kaworma, thanked the state government for awarding the contracts to their companies. They pledged to deliver quality infrastructure in line with approved specifications and contractual provisions, assuring that the projects would be completed within the agreed periods. The seven road projects were approved by the State Executive Council at its last meeting presided over by Governor Yahaya. They include the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, with a spur to Dalawaja, and Phase One of the four-kilometre Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road. Others are the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak; the 15-kilometre Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road; and the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road. The remaining projects are the 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road and the 1.5-kilometre Kunuwal Road Network. The latest contracts add to the administration’s ongoing efforts to expand the state’s road network, improve connectivity between rural and urban communities and enhance access to economic opportunities. The projects are expected to ease transportation challenges, facilitate the movement of farm produce to markets, reduce travel difficulties and improve economic activities across the benefiting communities upon completion. items.title: COP31: Onuigbo tasks legislators on climate laws, funding
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The President of GLOBE Legislators International, Rt. Hon. Sir Sam Ifeanyi Onuigbo, has urged parliamentarians across the world to translate international climate agreements into enforceable national laws, backed by adequate funding and effective oversight. Onuigbo said international climate agreements would achieve little unless national parliaments incorporated decisions reached at United Nations climate conferences into domestic legislation and ensured their implementation. He made the call at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) COP31 Parliamentary Meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, where he highlighted the role of legislators in ensuring that commitments reached at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of the Parties (COPs) produced tangible results at the national level. In a statement made available to journalists in Gombe on Saturday, the former member of the House of Representatives said parliamentarians must deploy their constitutional powers of lawmaking, budgetary appropriation and oversight to ensure governments implement international climate commitments. Drawing on his legislative experience, Onuigbo recalled that his participation in the GLOBE COP21 Legislators Summit in Paris influenced his decision to sponsor Nigeria’s Climate Change Act. He argued that without the necessary legislative backing, negotiations and agreements reached at international climate conferences could fail to translate into practical outcomes. “After all the contributions here, if they are not brought down into laws for implementation, it becomes an exercise in futility,” he said. Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation. He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight. Describing the deliberations at the Antalya meeting as detailed and incisive, he said their impact would ultimately depend on the ability of parliamentarians to translate the discussions into actionable legislation. The GLOBE Legislators president also commended the National Council on Climate Change, its leadership under Dr Majekodunmi, researchers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the development of the Host Country Approval Criteria for Carbon Market Activities in Nigeria and the country’s broader climate change efforts. He also acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s role in Nigeria’s climate change efforts. “Above all, I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who has exercised admirable leadership in ensuring that the climate journey remains steady and very successful,” he said. Onuigbo was inaugurated as President of GLOBE Legislators at the United Kingdom Parliament on June 24, 2026. Established in 1991, GLOBE Legislators works to strengthen parliamentary engagement and international cooperation on environmental governance and climate change. items.title: COP31 ou flop31?
items.description: La COP31 a ouvert ses portes ce lundi 9 et les a fermées ce dimanche 22 novembre, comme il fallait s'y attendre…sans accord. C'était à à Antalya en Turquie. Encore une autre COP, est-on tenté de dire. Certes, elle avait affiché la noble ambition de se pencher sur le véritable grand corps malade qu’est devenu la terre. Mais la santé de la maison est si intimement liée au intérêts des riches et puissants de ce monde qui ne pensent qu'industrialisation à outrance, que la montagne, comme à l'accoutumée, a accouchée, d'une souris, ou a, plutît, fait une fausse couche! La santé de la maison commune ne fera donc que se dégrader, tirant vers une agonie peut-être encore lente, mais certaine, en l'absence de tout traitement de choc. Une fois de plus, les spécialistes et autres experts du climat se sont réunis, pour discuter des options à mettre en œuvre pour parvenir à la protection des forêts, la conservation des océans et des glaciers, la priorisation des énergies alternatives au détriment de celles fossiles. Le combat contre l’agression de l’environnement par les sociétés minières a été remis au goût du jour, etc. Mais tout a été dit du bout des lèvres. Même le drapeau rouge qui a été brandi contre les mauvaises pratiques contre l'environnement, agité par le vent de la hantise exacerbée de la destruction continue de la couche d’ozone, fût sans effet. Une fois de plus, le slogan timide et encore vain de «pollueur payeur» a été asséné, sans sans faire frémir les destructeurs de l'atmosphére que nous avons héritée de nos dévanciers et que nous devons léguer aux gé. Et pour boucler la boucle, les engagements s’enfileront aux promesses peu ou prou tenues, le tout jalousement gardé pour être réchauffé à l’occasion des prochains sommets sur le réchauffement climatique. Donc, pendant deux semaines et plus de 48 heures de temps additionnel de discussions, il faudra encore placer tous les espoires sur les COP N+beaucoup à venir et dont le sort n'est pas certain d'être plus enviable., Et pendant les mêmes sujets ont, et seront, ressassés en terre turque, et seront encore triturés et retriturés lors des prichaines rencontres sur le climat, les populations africaines ne savent plus à quel saint se vouer. Les agriculteurs, les plus impactés par le dérèglement climatique, demeurent dépendants des caprices pluviométriques, scrutant à longueur de journée le ciel, implorant leurs dieux pour favoriser de bonnes récoltes. Mais, presque toujours, les résultats des efforts produits par les cultivateurs sont très en deçà de leurs prévisions, entraînant l’inévitable déficit alimentaire, voire la famine sous certains cieux. Et les gouvernements sont contraints de tendre la sébile auprès des partenaires techniques et financiers et «pays amis», pour juguler le manque et soulager le peuple. Malheureusement, les aides qui pleuvaient à une certaine époque sont maintenant distillées, à dose homéopathique. Les petits acteurs du secteur informel et les industriels déjà assommés par les coupures d’électricité récurrentes, ressentent nécessairement le coup de la mauvaise passe des agriculteurs, surtout quand, au gré du marché international, le coût du baril monte, souvent en flèche, provoquant la hausse, à la pompe, des prix du pétrole, de l’essence et du gazole. Cette augmentation se répercute systématiquement sur les coûts du transport, des denrées alimentaires, du loyer. En somme «tout augmente» comme le chante, en pleurant, le citoyen lambda. Dans cette triste logique, le panier de la ménagère se ratatine sans cesse. La vie chère s’installe alors. Et c’est la galère pour le consommateur! Véritables marronniers de l’actualité, les COPs se suivent donc et se ressemblent par l’inadéquation criarde entre la prise des résolutions et leur application sur le terrain. Car l’appétit gargantuesque des grandes puissances, dont la Chine et les Etats-Unis, n’a d’égale que l’impuissance des pays comme ceux africains, qui ploient le plus sous le poids du réchauffement climatique, alors qu’ils en sont, de loin, les moins fautifs. Si la COP31 n'a pas apporté un mieux pour la santé de la maison commune, que faut-il attendre de celles à venir pour le quotidien des populations africaines? Aucun optimisme n'est de mise! En plus d’être peu suffisante, la part de financement qui parvient au continent pour la lutte contre le changement climatique est détournée par des dirigeants aux intérêts personnels. Dans le même temps, les véritables coupables de la destruction de la couche d’ozone s’obstinent dans le sens du toujours plus d’industrie. Finalement, la potion magique tarde à sortir de la marmite des druides de la COP, ce qui corse l’équation de la crise du climat. Par Wakat Séra L’article COP31 ou flop31? est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Ouagadougou-Libreville: Air Burkina renoue avec le ciel gabonais
items.description: La compagnie aérienne nationale Air Burkina a officiellement repris, le samedi 21 novembre 2026, sa liaison aérienne entre Ouagadougou et Libreville, via Cotonou. Le vol 2J591, qui a marqué cette reprise, avait à son bord une délégation burkinabè conduite par le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE. Cette relance renforce les possibilités de mobilité entre les deux pays et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour les échanges économiques et la coopération régionale. La cérémonie officielle d’accueil du vol inaugural s’est déroulée à l’Aéroport International Léon-Mba de Libreville, en présence du Secrétaire Général du ministère gabonais des Affaires étrangères, de diplomates du Mali, du Niger, du Togo, du Bénin et du Sénégal, ainsi que des autorités aéroportuaires et de partenaires institutionnels. La délégation burkinabè comprenait également le Président du Conseil d’administration de Air Burkina, le Camarade Dr Drissa SAWADOGO et le Directeur Général de la compagnie, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE. Au nom du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Conseiller technique, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a salué une reprise qui constitue un levier important pour la mobilité des personnes, le développement économique et l’intégration africaine. Il y voit également une nouvelle étape dans le raffermissement des relations entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon. « La reprise de cette liaison directe entre le Burkina Faso et la République du Gabon marque une nouvelle étape de notre excellente relation d’amitié, de fraternité et de solidarité qui unissent nos deux nations », a-t-il soutenu. Le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a, en outre, exprimé la reconnaissance du Gouvernement burkinabè aux autorités gabonaises pour leur disponibilité et leur engagement en faveur du renforcement des échanges bilatéraux. Pour le Directeur Général de Air Burkina, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, cette reprise traduit la volonté de la compagnie nationale de consolider son réseau et de faciliter les déplacements entre les peuples africains. « A travers son réseau, notre compagnie entend poursuivre sa mission de rapprochement des peuples, de facilitation de la mobilité et de renforcement des échanges entre les nations africaines », a-t-il déclaré. Le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, a, par ailleurs, réitéré l’engagement de Air Burkina à assurer la régularité et la pérennité de cette desserte, dans le respect des exigences de sécurité, de ponctualité, de régularité et de qualité du service. Il a également salué les connexions aériennes entretenues avec plusieurs pays de la sous-région, notamment le Mali, le Sénégal, le Togo, le Bénin et le Niger. L’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso au Gabon, le Camarade Issa BORO, a, pour sa part, inscrit cette reprise dans la dynamique de renforcement de la coopération bilatérale. Il a notamment rappelé l’ouverture, en 2026, d’une Ambassade résidente du Gabon à Ouagadougou, ainsi que la tenue de la réunion des experts préparatoire à la deuxième session de la Grande commission mixte de coopération entre les deux pays. « Les travaux de cette réunion ont abouti à l’élaboration d’une vingtaine de projets d’accord qui seront validés ultérieurement par la réunion ministérielle », a-t- il précisé. Avec deux vols par semaine via Cotonou, la reprise de la liaison Ouagadougou-Libreville vient ainsi renforcer la connectivité aérienne entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale. Elle offre de nouvelles possibilités de déplacement aux voyageurs et contribue à faciliter les échanges entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon. DCRP/MATM L’article Ouagadougou-Libreville: Air Burkina renoue avec le ciel gabonais est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: External debt servicing will create depreciatory pressure on cedi in 2027
items.description: Fitch Solutions is warning that external debt service will generate depreciatory pressure on the cedi in 2027. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects external debt-service payments of roughly US$5.05 billion, up from US$4.7 billion in 2026. Meanwhile, the government’s 2027 Fiscal Strategy rules out Eurobond issuance until 2030 and caps project-loan disbursements, while Ghana’s Extended Credit Facility ended in July 2026. The UK-based firm said that although the reactivated Dollar Sinking Fund will likely cover around US$1.2 billion in Eurobond repayments, the remaining US$3.9 billion owed to multilateral, bilateral and commercial creditors will thus directly weigh on foreign exchange reserves. “This will drive the BoG [Bank of Ghana] to rebuild its reserves towards its Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP) targets, limiting its willingness to supply dollars to the market and creating a further headwind for the cedi”, it explained. Risks To Outlook Fitch Solutions said the risks are mixed but skewed to a weaker cedi in 2027. “ Dollar supply depends closely on gold, so a sharper fall in prices than our US$4,200/oz [per ounce] forecast, or disruptions to GoldBod’s exports, would quickly reduce flows to the FX [foreign exchange] market”, it stressed. Furthermore, it said a renewed flare-up in the US-Iran conflict would raise the oil import bill. In addition, the February 2027 redemption of domestic bonds could also see more cedi liquidity switched into dollars than expected as a result of low domestic Treasury yields. On the upside, Fitch Solutions said a further lift in gold prices towards US$5,000 per ounce, or BoG action to drain excess liquidity and lift market rates, would ease pressure on the cedi.

items.title: Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027. Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were temporary, arguing that Tinubu should be allowed to complete the foundation he had laid for Nigeria’s economic recovery and prosperity. The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State. He said Nigeria had been facing the threat of economic collapse before Tinubu assumed office, describing the president as courageous for taking difficult decisions. “This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” Wike said. “And that is why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done.” Wike cited what he described as improved stability in the university system, noting that strikes by lecturers over unpaid entitlements, which frequently disrupted academic calendars in the past, were no longer a recurring feature under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously encountered in accessing their entitlements, arguing that decisions taken by the president had helped address some of the country’s longstanding challenges. The FCT minister urged Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, insisting that the president’s campaign would accommodate Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said. Wike also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in appointments under the Tinubu administration, insisting that Christians had enjoyed greater representation in the current government than in previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” he said. The minister, during the service, announced a donation of N100 million to the church on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates. items.title: Des éléments armés du polisario encerclés en Mauritanie
items.description: Des éléments armés du polisario, venus du territoire algérien, seraient pris en étau par l'armée mauritanienne depuis le vendredi 20 novembre, d'après des sources des camps de Tindouf. L'affaire, rapportée par des sources proches des camps de Tindouf, concerne une formation du polisario baptisée « Brigade de réserve ». Ses hommes auraient franchi la frontière depuis l'Algérie et progressé de plusieurs kilomètres à l'intérieur du territoire mauritanien, avant d'être cernés par des unités de l'armée de ce pays. Depuis le vendredi 20 novembre, ils seraient maintenus sous contrôle, sans pouvoir ni avancer ni rebrousser chemin. D'après les mêmes sources, les forces mauritaniennes ont demandé aux membres du groupe armé de leur remettre les clés des voitures et du camion à bord desquels ils circulaient, ce que le groupe a fait, avant de leur demander de rendre leurs armes et leurs munitions. Les éléments armés issus du polisario ont refusé et réclamé un délai pour contacter leur direction à Rabouni en Algérie. Les sources ajoutent que ces éléments encerclés ont reçu du soi-disant ministère de la Défense du Front séparatiste l'instruction d'attendre et de ne pas remettre leurs armes jusqu'à de nouveaux ordres. Cet épisode survient dans un contexte de vigilance accrue le long de la frontière nord de la Mauritanie. L'Agence mauritanienne d'information (AMI) a rapporté la visite du wali de la région de Tiris Zemmour, Idrissa Demba Kourera, dans le département de Bir Oum Greïn. Il était accompagné du directeur général de l'Agence mauritanienne des mines, Mohamed Yahya Ould Ahmed Ghazi. Les deux responsables ont signifié aux orpailleurs artisanaux qu'ils devaient quitter, sous quatorze jours au plus, les sites d'exploitation traditionnelle situés à moins de dix kilomètres de la frontière. D'après l'AMI, qui en a fait état le mardi 17 novembre, le wali a pris une décision exigeant l'évacuation de tous les sites d'orpaillage artisanal situés dans une bande frontalière de dix kilomètres de profondeur. Il a justifié la mesure par le renforcement de la sécurité aux frontières et la nécessité de permettre aux forces armées de protéger le territoire, ainsi que par la protection des orpailleurs, qu'il s'agit d'éloigner de zones frontalières susceptibles de connaître des mouvements militaires ou des risques sécuritaires. Certains orpailleurs se sont dits prêts à s'y conformer, tout en réclamant un délai supplémentaire pour déplacer leurs équipements. Dans ce contexte, les mouvements des milices du polisario aux abords de la frontière mauritanienne subissent une pression croissante, Nouakchott se montrant intransigeante face à toute présence armée non autorisée sur son sol et attachée à son droit de protéger sa souveraineté et la sécurité de ses frontières. D'après ces mêmes médias mauritaniens, ces développements surviennent à la suite de mouvements militaires après des tentatives d'éléments du polisario de s'approcher de positions militaires marocaines. Les Forces armées royales auraient ciblé les éléments du polisario à Kleibat El Foula et à Oum Rouissine, en réponse à une tentative des milices du Front séparatiste de viser deux zones proches du mur de défense. The post Des éléments armés du polisario encerclés en Mauritanie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Government’s key test in managing debt lies in 2027 – KPMG UNDP report
items.description: The KPMG UNDP 2027 Budget Highlights says the government’s key test in managing Ghana’s public debt lies in 2027, when about GH¢53 billion of Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) obligations and US$1.17 billion of Eurobond payments fall due. The Cedi Sinking Fund held GH¢29 billion as at 11 November 2026, enough to cover the February 2027 principal (now offered for early redemption), while the US Dollar Sinking Fund is projected to reach about US$600 million by December 2026. According to the highlights, sustaining monthly Sinking Fund transfers (7% of non-oil tax revenue), lengthening the domestic maturity profile and keeping debt near the 45% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) anchor will be critical as the deficit widens to 2.9% of GDP in 2027. Ghana’s 2027 Budget shows that the country’s debt position remains stable, although the KPMG/UNDP report warned that significant repayment obligations for 2027 will test the durability of the debt management framework, anchored on the fiscal consolidation achieved in 2025 and sustained through 2026. As of end-October 2026, provisional total public debt stood at GH¢759.3 billion (US$65.3 billion), up from GH¢641.1 billion (US$61.3 billion) at end-2025. “Although the debt-to-GDP ratio rose to 47.5% from 44.7% at the end of 2025, it remains well below the 61.6% recorded at the end of 2024 and the ECOWAS convergence ceiling of 70%. The 18.4% increase in the debt stock was driven mainly by domestic debt, which rose by 28.2% to GH¢427.9 billion, while external debt increased by 7.8% to GH¢331.4 billion. Domestic debt now accounts for 56.4% of total public debt (external: 43.6%), consistent with the government’s strategy to reduce external exposure and limit exchange rate valuation effects”, the report said. Similarly, lower Treasury bill rates kept interest payments in October 2026 at GH¢38.8 billion, 24.7% below target, it mentioned The 2026 Debt Sustainability Analysis rates Ghana’s risk of external and overall debt distress as moderate, supporting rating upgrades by Fitch (‘B’) and Moody’s (‘B3’) in 2026. The report added that the government has remained current on its restructured obligations, paying GH¢10.8 billion to DDEP bondholders in August 2026 (GH¢41.36 billion since 2025) and US$700 million to Eurobond holders in July 2026 (US$2.1 billion since 2025). Bilateral restructuring agreements have been signed with 16 of 24 official creditor countries, with four more expected by the end of December 2026, alongside four commercial debt agreements. But the report stated that the actual test lies in 2027.

items.title: Accident en mer : les corps des deux pêcheurs disparus repêchés
items.description: ​Selon des sources concordantes, les opérations de ratissage menées par les secours et les pêcheurs locaux ont permis de localiser et de remonter les dépouilles des pêcheurs disparus dans la journée de ce Samedi 21 novembre 2026. ​ Le drame s'était noué en pleine mer lorsque l’embarcation artisanale a été heurtée par une barge de Bel Air Mining naviguant dans la zone. Sous la violence du choc, la pirogue avait chaviré, précipitant ses occupants à l'eau. Seul le capitaine, Abdoulaye Sylla, a eu la vie sauve, secouru in extremis, mais Abdoulaye Camara et Abdoulaye Kokoti Camara ont perdu la vie. ​« La barge s’est rapprochée d’eux et s’est accrochée à leurs filets, entraînant la pirogue vers le navire. L’un d’eux, qui cherchait son couteau, en a profité pour sauter à l’eau et a pu être sauvé. Les deux autres se sont retrouvés sous la barge et y ont malheureusement perdu la vie. Hier, le premier corps a été retrouvé et inhumé à 19 heures. Ce samedi, le deuxième corps a également été repêché près de la barge », a expliqué Fodé Idrissa Kallo, responsable des relations extérieures et de la communication de la Fédération nationale de la pêche artisanale de Guinée (FENAPAG). items.title: Souveraineté et haute technologie : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré dote le Burkina Faso d’un joyau académique en 11 mois chrono
items.description: Conçue pour inscrire le Burkina Faso sur la voie de la souveraineté scientifique et industrielle, l’Académie technologique du Faso (ATF) est désormais prête à accueillir sa toute première promotion. Érigé en un temps record de 11 mois sur un domaine de 60 hectares dans la commune de Babray, ce complexe universitaire ultramoderne sous régime d'internat intégral sera officiellement inauguré ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Rattachée directement à la Présidence, l'institution forme 250 jeunes lauréats scientifiques dans des filières stratégiques allant du génie civil au nucléaire civil. C'est une étape décisive pour l'histoire industrielle et académique du pays des Hommes intègres. Inspecté en décembre 2025 par le chef de l'État, le chantier de l'Académie technologique du Faso (ATF), implanté sur la voie de contournement dans la commune de Babray, a vu les engins entrer en action dès janvier 2026. Alors qu'un délai de réalisation de 12 mois était initialement prévu, il a suffi de juste 11 mois pour achever la première phase de ce complexe de 60 hectares sous un contrôle-qualité rigoureux. Ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, l'infrastructure est officiellement inaugurée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, scellant la concrétisation d'une ambition présidentielle majeure. Le nouveau campus a été conçu pour rompre définitivement avec les enseignements purement théoriques. En quelques mois, le site s'est métamorphosé pour accueillir des amphithéâtres connectés, des ateliers de pointe, une forge industrielle, une bibliothèque, une infirmerie et des infrastructures sportives. Fonctionnant sous un régime d'internat intégral, l'académie garantit l'hébergement sur place des étudiants comme des enseignants, créant un cadre de vie axé sur la discipline, la cohésion et l'excellence. Directement rattachée à la Présidence du Faso, l'institution prépare les élèves aux métiers de demain dans des secteurs clés tels que la métallurgie, le génie civil, la chimie industrielle et les métiers miniers, tout en ouvrant la voie au nucléaire civil, à l'aéronautique, à la cybersécurité et au digital. Pour intégrer cette école d'élite, la sélection a exigé un niveau académique exceptionnel. Dès juillet 2026, à la suite des résultats du baccalauréat, un processus rigoureux a permis de choisir 250 jeunes lauréats issus des séries scientifiques et techniques parmi des milliers de candidats. Soumis à une rigueur exigeante et encadrés par des formateurs chevronnés, ces pionniers ont vocation à concevoir les infrastructures futures, à piloter les transformations industrielles et à sécuriser les réseaux énergétiques et numériques du pays. En investissant sur son propre sol dans le talent de sa jeunesse, le Burkina Faso brise les chaînes de la dépendance extérieure. items.title: L'ancien président brésilien Jair Bolsonaro en soins intensif après une occlusion intestinale
items.description: L’ancien président brésilien Jair Bolsonaro, 71 ans, reste en soins intensifs pour une occlusion intestinale et son état est « cliniquement stable », a indiqué dimanche l’hôpital DF Star de Brasilia dans un bulletin qui ne précise pas de date de sortie. Admis vendredi 20 pour de fortes douleurs abdominales, M. Bolsonaro a été diagnostiqué samedi « d’une occlusion intestinale aiguë ». L’équipe médicale poursuit le traitement, qui comprend une mise à jeun et un soutien nutritionnel, selon l’hôpital. Dimanche matin, son épouse, Michelle Bolsonaro, a indiqué sur les réseaux sociaux qu’il avait passé la nuit « sans douleur », qu’il avait pu marcher et qu’il avait passé des examens d’imagerie. L’ancien chef de l’État a subi plusieurs opérations de l’abdomen depuis l’agression au couteau dont il a été victime pendant la campagne présidentielle de 2018. Avant son hospitalisation, il purgeait à domicile, pour raisons de santé, une peine de 27 ans et trois mois de prison pour son rôle dans la tentative de coup d’État qui a suivi sa défaite face à Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva à l’élection présidentielle de 2022. Sur le plan judiciaire, la Cour suprême examinera du 4 au 15 décembre quatre recours contestant la constitutionnalité d’une loi qui modifie le calcul des peines lorsque plusieurs infractions contre les institutions démocratiques sont commises dans un même contexte. L’issue de cet examen pourrait avoir une incidence sur la durée de la peine de l’ancien président. items.title: FIP Bronze S2 Accra: Ghana takes major step in Padel development with historic tournament
items.description: Ghana made history on Sunday as the first International Padel Federation Bronze tournament in the country successfully concluded at the S2 Sport Club in Spintex, Accra. The FIP Bronze S2 Accra, which offered world ranking points and entry into the professional circuit, ran for a week and crowned champions in both the men’s and women’s categories. Spain’s Adrian Lopez and Guillem Santiago claimed the men’s title after beating Egypt’s George Wakim and Morocco’s Mohamed Alami in straight sets. The Spanish pair won 6-4, 6-1 following a tougher semi-final earlier in the day. Santiago says he is already looking forward to returning to Ghana for the next edition. “Great tournament. Great crowd. Great organisation. It’s our first time here, and we enjoyed it a lot. I hope we will come back next year.” In the women’s category, Spain’s Cayetana Sanchez Vera and Greece’s Christina Ntanou also won the title with a straight-sets victory over France’s Cimille Siriex and the Netherlands’ Tess de Vocht. They won 6-3, 6-4 after cruising to a 6-1, 6-1 semi-final victory. The victory also marked a personal milestone for Vera and Ntanou, who claimed their first international medals in Ghana. For Professional Padel Association of Ghana president Jean Noel Said, the tournament has already made a significant impact on the growth of the sport in the country. “It means improvement, growth and development because we started padel in Ghana four years ago, and today we’re hosting the first FIP Bronze tournament in the country. I think it shows that the community is growing and that there’s an interest in the sport in Ghana. “We want to give the youth an opportunity to see what the pros are doing, how they’re performing and how they’re playing. I think it’s a great opportunity for them. The kids really enjoyed it. They were interacting with the pros, asking questions and playing with them, so I think it was a great move.” His vice-president, Nour Seklaoui, added: “Two years ago, when the federation was formed, nobody thought we would get here that quickly. Part of our mission and vision was to achieve this, and we can see now that the sky is the limit. If we’re able to host an FIP Bronze tournament in just two years, you never know when we will host Silver and then Gold tournaments. This is a great achievement for Ghana.” The tournament ended on a celebratory note, with the medal ceremony turning into a birthday celebration for Said and Moroccan player Mohamed Alami. From medal celebrations to a birthday party The International Padel Federation Bronze S2 Accra women’s tournament medal ceremony took a celebratory turn as the Padel Association of Ghana President, Jean Noel Said, marked his birthday. #JoySports https://t.co/SDLJiUVJqj — #JoySports (@JoySportsGH) November 22, 2026

items.title: « La Guinée ne saurait oublier Petit Sory » : un symposium organisé par le gouvernement en présence des anciennes gloires du football
items.description: Le gouvernement guinéen a organisé ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026 un symposium pour rendre un ultime hommage à Petit Sory, décédé le 21 novembre. La cérémonie a réuni des membres du gouvernement, d'anciennes gloires du football guinéen, membres de la famille et proches collaborateurs du défunt. Le ministre des Sports, Cellou Baldé, a présenté les condoléances des autorités à la famille éplorée: « Je suis là au nom du gouvernement de la République, au nom du Premier ministre, Chef du gouvernement Monsieur Amadou Oury Bah, au nom du président de la République Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi Doumbouya, pour présenter solennellement et officiellement, les condoléances du Président, du gouvernement et de l'ensemble des institutions de la République à la famille biologique et sportive de feu Petit Sory » , a-t-il déclaré. Lors du symposium, il a placé Petit Sory et ses coéquipiers dans la lignée des grandes figures de l'histoire nationale : « Petit Sory et ses coéquipiers, pour moi, c'est comme ceux qui nous ont conduit vers l'indépendance. C'est comme Almamy Samory Touré, c'est comme Zébela Togba Pivi, c'est comme Dinah Salifou, c'est comme Alpha Yaya Diallo, parce que la fibre, elle est la même : c'est la patrie. C'est ce qui les a animés » , a-t-il souligné. Il a insisté sur la portée des exploits des anciens du Hafia : « La période post-indépendance pendant laquelle les anciens du Hafia ont posé ces actes héroïques, c'était une période particulière. Période pendant laquelle ces actes héroïques posés n'étaient pas qu'un simple jeu de sport ou de football. Cela nous a permis de renforcer notre souveraineté et d'asseoir davantage la respectabilité de notre pays à l'échelle continentale et internationale, parce que c'était aussi un enjeu politique et un enjeu géopolitique » , a-t-il expliqué. Il a ensuite lancé : « Et donc, la Guinée ne saurait oublier Petit Sory. La Guinée ne saurait oublier toutes ces gloires, tous ces amis et coéquipiers de Petit Sory. » Cellou Baldé a par ailleurs indiqué que les doléances formulées lors de la rencontre, par les anciennes gloires du Hafia avaient été entendues : « Nous avons aussi écouté attentivement. Nous avons compris toutes les doléances formulées. Nous allons travailler à les mettre en œuvre au niveau du ministère des Sports, en relation bien entendu avec la Fédération guinéenne de football, mais nous transmettrons fidèlement les doléances au Premier ministre, chef du gouvernement, et au président de la République » , a-t-il laissé entendre. Il a enfin fait le lien entre l'hommage rendu aux anciens et l'action actuelle des autorités : « Si aujourd'hui nous sommes en train de jouer au stade du 28-Septembre, c'est aussi une manière de rendre hommage aux anciens du Hafia 77. […] C'est le rayonnement de la Guinée, c'est le Hafia 77 qui revit aujourd'hui », a-t-il conclu .

items.title: NELFUND considers increase in ₦20,000 student upkeep
items.description: …Sawyer says allowance under review, hints at possible changes By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is considering an increase in its ₦20,000 monthly upkeep allowance for students amid concerns that rising living costs have reduced its purchasing power. The Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headlines, saying the allowance was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new amount or timeline for any adjustment, Sawyer confirmed that the possibility of an increase was being considered. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The proposed review comes amid complaints by students that the current allowance is inadequate to meet the rising costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs. Sawyer, however, said any increase would have to take into account the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for all eligible beneficiaries. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” he said. Beyond the proposed review, the NELFUND chief disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to provide students with more substantial financial support to help them complete their academic programmes. He did not provide details of the proposed intervention, including its scope, funding or implementation timeline. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” Sawyer said. He also hinted that changes could be introduced in the future, although he gave no definite commitment on when the review would be concluded. “I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added. NELFUND’s proposed review comes as the Federal Government’s student loan scheme continues to expand, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance for tertiary education. According to figures provided by the fund, it has disbursed ₦180.5 billion in upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another ₦194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees. The combined disbursement of approximately ₦375.2 billion underscores the scale of the programme, which is intended to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and help students remain in school. The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions. Despite the programme’s expansion, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a concern for beneficiaries who depend on it to meet their daily expenses. For now, the ₦20,000 monthly allowance remains unchanged, pending any formal announcement by NELFUND or the Federal Government on a possible increase or additional intervention. items.title: Capital per worker in Ghana slows to 1.0% per year, job quality lags – GSS
items.description: Capital per worker in Ghana slows to 1.0% per year, job quality lags – GSS The Ghana Statistical Service has revealed in its 2026 Productivity, Employment and Growth Report that the growth in capital per worker has slowed to 1.0% per year since 2020. During the same period, productivity growth has also slowed. In the report, the GSS said productivity gains are uneven across sectors. Accordingly, information and communication recorded the fastest productivity growth, and electricity and gas the fastest employment growth, but both employ relatively few people. However, agriculture remains the largest employer and has the lowest output per worker, at GH₵8,859 in 2025. Manufacturing has held steady at about 10% of Gross Domestic Product, while its employment grew by about 5.0% to 6.0% a year. The report further revealed that more people are working, but job quality has lagged. Employment rose from 11.1 million in 2021 to 13.3 million in 2025. Yet unemployment stands at 12.8%, and at 32.4% among young people aged 15 to 24 in the labour force. Close to one in five people aged 15 to 35 is NEET, at 17.9%. About 86% of workers are in informal employment (quarter 3 2025 only), 72.0% are in vulnerable employment (72.2% in quarter 3 2025), and 11.6% work fewer hours than they would like. Earnings below output per worker Also, earnings are below output per worker. In 2025, the average worker produced GH₵15,197 in value added and earned GH₵9,388. In industry, output per worker was GH₵30,588 and earnings were GH₵15,822. Average earnings remain below their level before the pandemic. The report added that earnings are below output per worker. In 2025, the average worker produced GH₵15,197 in value added and earned GH₵9,388. In industry, output per worker was GH₵30,588 and earnings were GH₵15,822. Average earnings remain below their level before the pandemic. What this means for policy The GSS said the evidence points to five priorities. First, productivity should be measured and reported as a national goal, since it is the main link between growth and higher incomes. Second, raising productivity where most people already work, in agriculture, trade, informal services and manufacturing, has the widest reach. Third, investment needs to recover and to be used better: growth driven by adding capital and labour has limits, and the next phase depends more on using existing resources well, through technology, skills, management and a more efficient allocation of resources. Fourth, young people’s skills need to be matched to available jobs, given high unemployment among secondary school leavers. Fifth, productivity gains should be linked to earnings and decent work through wage-setting mechanisms and social dialogue, since that determines whether growth improves living standards. The second edition of the Productivity, Employment and Growth Report answered both questions for Ghana over 35 years, from 1991 to 2025. It combined the national accounts with four censuses and surveys, and followed methods set by the International Labour Organization and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development.

items.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
items.description: Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years, Maxx Morando, during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California. A string of black-and-white photos the singer shared on Instagram showed the pair kissing, surrounded by white roses. Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, appeared in the background of one image. Her father, Billy Ray Cyrus, was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley. Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said “I do” in a black suit from the same fashion house. In one of the photographs, the first in a series the singer shared on Instagram, the newlyweds posed next to a golden retriever. The post was captioned with “M+M” followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November. Miley’s sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments. The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra. Guests reportedly stuck to an all-black dress code. The American singer confirmed her engagement to the 28-year-old drummer during an interview with US TV show Good Morning America last year. She said Morando had got down on one knee for the proposal during a trip to Asia. “I am not easy to surprise because I love to control every situation and I had completely surrendered and I’m telling you, I was so, so, so surprised,” she said. During an interview with Wonderland, Morando said he “had to be really sneaky” to keep his proposal plans a secret. “We went to Tokyo first for a couple days, and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could,” he said. Cyrus, 33, had previously been married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth but the couple separated in 2019. The singer, whose hits include Party in the U.S.A and Wrecking Ball, married Hunger Games star Hemsworth in 2018 after the couple were in a relationship for a decade. Speaking to British Vogue in 2023, Cyrus said she and 28-year-old Morando met after being “put on a blind date”. Morando is a drummer with LA-based band Liily. The band participated in NBC’s Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party – hosted by Cyrus – in 2022, alongside musicians including Cyrus’s late godmother Dolly Parton and David Byrne.

items.title: Australia’s Sanctions on West Bank Settlers Increase Pressure
items.description: Click to expand Image Israeli forces fire tear gas at Palestinians and journalists covering military operations and settler activity in the nearby village of Tal, in the West Bank, July 25, 2026. © 2026 Roman Levin/Sipa via AP Photo Australia announced on November 18 further targeted sanctions on three individuals and four entities involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank. Although these sanctions are a welcome step, they are long overdue and don’t go far enough. The situation in the West Bank is dire. State-backed settler violence has risen to all-time highs. Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been displaced and 1,394 killed by settlers or soldiers in the West Bank since the start of 2023. The number of illegal Israeli settlements has nearly doubled, including the E1 settlement project, which even Israel’s allies have called a “red line,” and which Israeli ministers openly boast is intended to erase any possibility of a future Palestinian state. On the same day as Australia’s announcement, the United Kingdom announced sanctions against eight construction companies and property development firms that have not, until now, been sanctioned by any government. The individuals and companies sanctioned by Australia, however, have previously been sanctioned by the United Kingdom and other states. When the United Kingdom, France, and Canada announced a ban on Israel’s illegal settlements in September, Australia did not join. Instead, at the time, Foreign Minister Wong promised further sanctions to deter illegal settlement, which are the ones just announced. Israel’s settlements are illegal. In its 2024 advisory opinion, the International Court of Justice found that all states have an obligation to “take steps to prevent trade or investment relations that assist in the maintenance of the illegal situation created by Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.” Banning trade with illegal settlements isn’t optional. It’s required by international law. Australia says it is genuinely committed to upholding international law while continuing to trade with unlawful settlements that rob Palestinians of their land and livelihoods. Recent reporting suggested that the majority of agricultural shipments coming to Australia marked as “products of Israel” are from illegal settlements. It’s past time for Australia to do everything in its power to stop the expansion of settlements, both through a trade ban and targeted sanctions on construction companies engaged in illegal settlement expansion.

items.title: T-bills auction: Government records 16% undersubscription, but interest rates dip
items.description: The government recorded a 16% undersubscription of its Treasury bills to the tune of GH¢3.64 billion, but this could be a deliberate move by the Treasury to reduce the cost of borrowing. According to the Bank of Ghana auction results, the auction target was GH¢4.25 billion. However, the government accepted bids totaling GH¢3.1 billion, below the target. A little over GH¢2.3 billion of the bids came from the 91-day bill, representing 64.7% of the total bids. The uptake was about GH¢2.1 billion. The 182-day bill also received bids of about GH¢645.9 million. However, GH¢590.5 million was accepted. A little above GH¢636 million in bids were tendered for the 364-day bill. About GH¢401 million of the bids were accepted. Meanwhile, interest rates went down along the yield curve. The yield on the 91-day bill declined by 4.0 basis points to 4.51%. Also, the 182-day bill decreased to 6.11% from the preceding week’s 6.16%. Similarly, the yield on the 364-day bill eased by 2.0 basis points to 9.44%.

items.title: Atletico Madrid beat Getafe 3-0 to keep pressure on Barcelona, Real Madrid
items.description: Atletico Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday. Diego Simeone’s side, third, are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off second-place Real Madrid, who both won earlier this weekend. Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julian Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital. Alex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sorloth. “I think the team had a very good, serious game, in defence and attack,” Atletico playmaker Baena told Movistar. “We are focused on our own work, not looking at what Barcelona and Madrid are doing, and that suits us best.” The Rojiblancos moved ahead after 10 minutes, with Alvarez teeing up Baena on the edge of the box to drill home low and hard at the near post. Getafe goalkeeper David Soria saved well from Alvarez and David Hancko but was at fault for Atletico’s second goal. Soria missed his punch from Alvarez’s corner and United States international Cardoso turned home with his knee from point-blank range. Baena smashed over a fine chance for the third after Pablo Barrios played him in behind. Soria denied Baena in the second half and Lee Kang-in fired over as Atletico continued to control the game and defended solidly to keep Getafe, 17th, at bay. Atletico substitute Sorloth should have scored with a few minutes remaining but powered an effort straight at Soria. items.title: Russell Brand’s wife says she’ll honour prison rules after message row
items.description: The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will “honour” his prison’s rules, a week after she read a message from her husband claiming his innocence. Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms. She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend herself and her family against her portrayal in the media during the couple’s weekly podcast, which she now presents alone. Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault. “Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention,” Laura Brand said during this week’s episode of Sunday Service. “Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that.” In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was “not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for”. Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was “OK”. Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women. Further allegations have since been reported about him and some have called for consent laws to be revised . His conviction has renewed conversation about safeguarding in the media industry, and whether some celebrities are still able to use their fame to prey on women and then silence them. Ministers have pointed out that inmates are prohibited from making statements that are likely to cause their victims distress and have said Brand’s message was being investigated. A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16, but who was not among the women whose accusations led to his conviction, said his prison message was “upsetting” and “really shocking” . The government attempted to have the podcast removed from YouTube, but this was refused by its owner Google. Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged social media companies to “show some decency and take these videos down”. On Sunday, Laura Brand also said that Sunday Service would be a place where she would “continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media’s image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny”. She expressed feeling a mixture of “grief”, “absence”, “desolation” and “loneliness” since her husband’s imprisonment.

items.title: GAFM resolves regulatory status with GTEC, clarifies professional certification role
items.description: The Global Academy of Finance and Management (GAFM), USA, says it has resolved a regulatory discrepancy with the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) following engagements and the submission of documents on its international recognition and professional accreditations. In a press release dated November 23, 2026, the organisation said GTEC removed it from its list of unrecognised universities on August 28, 2026, and maintained the exclusion in its subsequent September, October and November directories. GAFM said the resolution reflects its status as an international professional certification body and standards organisation, rather than a university or an institution that awards academic degrees and diplomas. It stressed that it had never sought recognition in Ghana as an academic university and did not present its professional certifications as academic qualifications. According to the organisation, its certifications are designed to demonstrate specialised professional knowledge and competencies. The requirements may include relevant education, examinations, work experience, adherence to ethical standards and continuing professional development. GAFM said its credentials operate within the professional certification sector, citing designations administered by international bodies such as the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and Project Management Professional (PMP) as examples of professional credentials. It, however, emphasised that its certifications are not substitutes for academic degrees, government-issued licences or statutory examinations required by law. GAFM explains international quality certifications The organisation also highlighted its international quality certifications, including ISO 9001 for Quality Management Systems, ISO 21001 for Educational Organisations and ISO 29993 for Learning Services Outside Formal Education. It said the certifications provide independent verification of aspects of its quality management systems and learning services. GAFM clarified, however, that these standards do not amount to university accreditation. A representative of the organisation welcomed what it described as GTEC’s decision, saying the development would help ensure that professional credentials are properly distinguished from academic qualifications. The representative said GAFM supported the accurate classification of professional certification bodies, adding that the resolution would help protect the integrity of Ghana’s academic landscape and regulatory framework. The organisation said it remained committed to transparency and continued cooperation with GTEC on international quality assurance standards. GAFM issues professional certifications, chartered designations and continuing education credentials in finance, management and related fields. FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Download

items.title: Barcelona return top of La Liga with Villarreal win
items.description: Barcelona scored three goals in 10 minutes to return to the top of La Liga with a victory over Villarreal at Spotify Nou Camp. Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes, with Tajon Buchanan and a rifled effort from Tani Oluwaseyi, leaving the home fans stunned. It is the first time the Blaugrana have conceded twice in the opening seven minutes of a league match since November 1981, against Real Zaragoza. After 23 minutes, Oluwaseyi fouled Lamine Yamal in the box, and a penalty was awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) review, but the Spain international dragged it wide. Gerard Martin headed over from close range just before the break as Barcelona struggled to make the most of their chances. But Barca came out with more attacking intent in the second half, and Martin made amends, heading home from Pedri’s cross to reduce the deficit. Fermin Lopez slotted home from Lamine Yamal’s pass across the box to equalise for Hansi Flick’s side on the hour mark. Eric Garcia’s cross was turned into his own net by Villarreal defender Pau Navarro, giving Barca their first lead of the match in the 67th minute. Navarro’s afternoon worsened when he received a second yellow for a foul on Barca captain Raphinha in stoppage time. Villarreal manager Inigo Perez has now managed six matches against Barca without winning (one draw, five losses). Barca lead rivals Real Madrid by three points and face Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday (17:45 GMT).

items.title: Francis Amissah joins Martell’s Swift Academy in Accra
items.description: Ghanaian public relations consultant Francis Amissah, popularly known in entertainment circles as Banks, is set to participate in the Accra edition of Martell’s Swift Academy, an initiative aimed at supporting the development of emerging African creatives. Amissah, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Elite PR, brings more than a decade of experience in public relations and communications to the programme. Through Elite PR, he has worked with several artistes and entertainment personalities, including E.L, Wendy Shay, Zlatan, D-Black, the Mitch Brothers, Dulcie Boateng, Mark Asari and RCee. His work has focused on securing media coverage, strengthening the visibility of talent and connecting creatives with wider audiences. Amissah says the academy will provide an opportunity to exchange ideas, build industry connections and gain fresh perspectives to support his work in the creative sector. “I’m glad to be part of this experience. Beyond the opportunity to connect with people in the industry, I look forward to learning, exchanging ideas, and gaining new perspectives that will contribute to my growth and the work I do within the creative space,” he said. The Accra edition of the Swift Academy, created by Martell and curated by Africa House, is scheduled to run from November 22 to December 19, 2026. The programme will bring together selected creatives for mentorship sessions, masterclasses and other activities designed to encourage professional development and collaboration within Ghana’s creative industry. Its activities will include a welcome mixer, a group panel discussion, one-on-one mentorship sessions, a workshop day and a music showcase. The academy’s facilitators and resource persons include Ghanaian singer-songwriter Gyakie, rapper M.anifest, award-winning music producer Juls, cultural curator Maxwell Adjavon and talent manager Therese Akua Jones. Their sessions will draw on experience across music, talent development, cultural programming and the business of entertainment. For Amissah, participation in the programme offers an opportunity to broaden his professional network and deepen his understanding of the creative industry beyond his established work in public relations. The academy is expected to bring together emerging and established players in Ghana’s creative ecosystem for learning and collaboration.

items.title: Ouagadougou-Libreville : Air Burkina renoue avec le ciel gabonais
items.description: La compagnie aérienne nationale Air Burkina a officiellement repris, le samedi 21 novembre 2026, sa liaison aérienne entre Ouagadougou et Libreville, via Cotonou. Le vol 2J591, qui a marqué cette reprise, avait à son bord une délégation burkinabè conduite par le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE. Cette relance renforce les possibilités de mobilité entre les deux pays et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour les échanges économiques et la coopération régionale. La cérémonie officielle d’accueil du vol inaugural s’est déroulée à l’Aéroport International Léon-Mba de Libreville, en présence du Secrétaire Général du ministère gabonais des Affaires étrangères, de diplomates du Mali, du Niger, du Togo, du Bénin et du Sénégal, ainsi que des autorités aéroportuaires et de partenaires institutionnels. La délégation burkinabè comprenait également le Président du Conseil d’administration de Air Burkina, le Camarade Dr Drissa SAWADOGO et le Directeur Général de la compagnie, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE. Au nom du Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Conseiller technique, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a salué une reprise qui constitue un levier important pour la mobilité des personnes, le développement économique et l’intégration africaine. Il y voit également une nouvelle étape dans le raffermissement des relations entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon. « La reprise de cette liaison directe entre le Burkina Faso et la République du Gabon marque une nouvelle étape de notre excellente relation d’amitié, de fraternité et de solidarité qui unissent nos deux nations », a-t-il soutenu. Le Conseiller technique du Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Jean Victorien TOE, a, en outre, exprimé la reconnaissance du Gouvernement burkinabè aux autorités gabonaises pour leur disponibilité et leur engagement en faveur du renforcement des échanges bilatéraux. Pour le Directeur Général de Air Burkina, le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, cette reprise traduit la volonté de la compagnie nationale de consolider son réseau et de faciliter les déplacements entre les peuples africains. « A travers son réseau, notre compagnie entend poursuivre sa mission de rapprochement des peuples, de facilitation de la mobilité et de renforcement des échanges entre les nations africaines », a-t-il déclaré. Le Camarade Wendkuni Serge Frédéric ZOMBRE, a, par ailleurs, réitéré l’engagement de Air Burkina à assurer la régularité et la pérennité de cette desserte, dans le respect des exigences de sécurité, de ponctualité, de régularité et de qualité du service. Il a également salué les connexions aériennes entretenues avec plusieurs pays de la sous-région, notamment le Mali, le Sénégal, le Togo, le Bénin et le Niger. L’Ambassadeur du Burkina Faso au Gabon, le Camarade Issa BORO, a, pour sa part, inscrit cette reprise dans la dynamique de renforcement de la coopération bilatérale. Il a notamment rappelé l’ouverture, en 2026, d’une Ambassade résidente du Gabon à Ouagadougou, ainsi que la tenue de la réunion des experts préparatoire à la deuxième session de la Grande commission mixte de coopération entre les deux pays. « Les travaux de cette réunion ont abouti à l’élaboration d’une vingtaine de projets d’accord qui seront validés ultérieurement par la réunion ministérielle », a-t- il précisé. Avec deux vols par semaine via Cotonou, la reprise de la liaison Ouagadougou-Libreville vient ainsi renforcer la connectivité aérienne entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale. Elle offre de nouvelles possibilités de déplacement aux voyageurs et contribue à faciliter les échanges entre le Burkina Faso et le Gabon. items.title: Entretien périodique de l’axe Pâ-Dano-Diébougou : Le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé constate des imperfections et exige une rigueur absolue
items.description: En route ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 pour le lancement des travaux du tronçon Batié-Kpuéré-frontière Côte d'Ivoire sur la RN11, le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, le camarade Mikaïlou Sidibé, a effectué plusieurs arrêts d'inspection sur le chantier d'entretien périodique de la RN12, reliant Pâ, Dano et Diébougou. Confronté à des zones de dégradations précoces causées par des défauts de portance de la chaussée, le ministre, accompagné du conseiller spécial du président du Faso, Roland Somda, a rassuré les usagers : l’ensemble des imperfections sera impérativement traité par l'entreprise adjudicataire avant toute réception des travaux. L'exigence de qualité dans la réalisation des infrastructures publiques ne tolère aucun compromis. Ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, alors qu'il se rendait au lancement du chantier de construction et de bitumage du tronçon Batié-Kpuéré-frontière Côte d'Ivoire sur la RN11, le ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, le camarade Mikaïlou Sidibé, a marqué plusieurs arrêts le long de la RN12. Accompagné du ministre conseiller spécial du président du Faso chargé de la construction, le camarade Roland Somda, et de ses collaborateurs techniques, le ministre a tenu à observer directement l’état d’avancement et la conformité des travaux en cours sur la section Pâ–Dano–Diébougou. Les interventions menées sur la RN12 s’inscrivent dans un programme spécifique d'entretien périodique. Le projet consiste en un resurfaçage de la chaussée au moyen d'un enrobé bitumineux de 5 cm d'épaisseur, et non d'une réhabilitation lourde globale. Le chantier comprend également le traitement structurant des traversées d'agglomération au niveau de Pâ, Founzan, Dano, Djikologo et Diébougou. Dans ces localités, les aménagements prévoient notamment l'élargissement à 2×2 voies à Dano, ainsi que des travaux d'assainissement et d’éclairage public destinés à sécuriser et moderniser le cadre de vie riverain. Au cours de l'inspection, la délégation ministérielle a arrêté son attention sur plusieurs zones présentant des dégradations anormales. Le ministre Mikaïlou Sidibé a expliqué que ces désordres proviennent d'une portance de la chaussée qui n'était pas uniforme sur l'ensemble du tronçon. Soucieux de préserver la durabilité de l'ouvrage, le ministre a affirmé que ces défaillances ont été clairement répertoriées et que l'entreprise exécutante apportera les traitements nécessaires pour corriger l'ensemble des imperfections constatées avant toute réception officielle des travaux. Réitérant la détermination de son département à veiller au respect strict des normes de qualité, le ministre a tenu à rassurer les usagers sur la livraison finale d'une route conforme aux exigences requises. items.title: Ashanti NDC Communications Officer Kabore endorses Dr Sammy Ayeh for Deputy National Communications Officer role
items.description: The newly elected Ashanti Regional Communications Officer of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mahmud Kabore, has endorsed Dr Sammy Ayeh for the position of Deputy National Communications Officer, urging party delegates to prioritise competence, experience and continuity in the forthcoming national executive elections. In a Facebook post on Friday, November 20, 2026, Mr Kabore drew parallels between Dr Ayeh’s candidature and the experience of the party’s former National Communications Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, who, he said, faced similar criticisms over his age and experience before his election in 2018. He argued that Mr Gyamfi’s eventual success demonstrated why party delegates should look beyond age and other criticisms when assessing candidates for leadership positions. “Thankfully, the delegates of our great party at the time demonstrated remarkable political wisdom. They refused to be swayed by name-calling, character assassination, smear campaigns and unsubstantiated allegations. Instead, they looked beyond age, recognised ability, rewarded dedication and voted overwhelmingly for competence,” he wrote. Mr Kabore said the experience should serve as a lesson to Dr Ayeh, whom he urged to remain focused on his campaign and allow his record of service and commitment to the party to speak for him. “My brother, Dr Sammy Ayeh, I share this history with you because I believe there are important lessons to be learnt from it. Do not be distracted by the noise. Remain focused, articulate your vision, engage the delegates and allow your record of service, competence and commitment to speak for you,” he stated. Kabore highlights Ayeh’s experience and party credentials In justifying his endorsement, the Ashanti Regional Communications Officer highlighted Dr Ayeh’s political and professional background, particularly his involvement in the NDC’s communication structures and student leadership. He cited Dr Ayeh’s tenure as President of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) at the University of Cape Coast (UCC), his contribution to the NDC National Communications Team and his role as the party’s Manifesto Spokesperson on Youth Development during the 2024 general elections. He also referenced Dr Ayeh’s current responsibilities in government communication and his role as host of the party’s weekly media platform, NDC 360. According to Mr Kabore, these experiences represent more than titles, providing Dr Ayeh with the institutional knowledge, exposure and practical experience required to occupy the deputy communications position. “These are not merely titles to decorate a political profile. They represent experience, exposure, institutional knowledge and years of demonstrated commitment to the communication machinery of our party,” he said. He argued that Dr Ayeh’s credentials, coupled with his vision and ability to build on the achievements of Mr Gyamfi’s administration as National Communications Officer, made a compelling case for his candidature. Mr Kabore, however, stressed that his endorsement was not intended to undermine the contributions or loyalty of other aspirants seeking the position. He said all candidates deserved respect, adding that the contest should be about identifying the person best positioned to ensure continuity, competence and innovation within the party’s communication machinery. “As we look towards consolidating our gains and preparing for the political battles ahead, we must elect leaders who understand the demands of the office, appreciate the foundations already laid and possess the capacity to take our communication front to even greater heights,” he added. He appealed to NDC delegates across the country to choose what he described as competence over sentiment, capacity over rhetoric, and continuity with innovation over unnecessary experimentation. Endorsement adds to growing support for Dr Ayeh Mr Kabore’s endorsement adds to a series of public declarations of support for Dr Ayeh’s candidature in recent weeks. On November 17, a coalition of medical practitioners and former student leaders publicly endorsed the presidential aide, citing his professional background, student leadership experience, political commitment and exposure to public administration. Earlier, on November 13, Presidential Staffer Beatrice Annan also endorsed his candidature, describing him as a capable individual with the potential to take on greater responsibilities. “You have demonstrated your ability, competence and potential, and we are all rooting for you,” she wrote in a Facebook post. Who is Dr Sammy Ayeh? Dr Sammy Ayeh is a medical doctor and political communicator who currently serves as a Presidential Aide responsible for Communications at the Office of the President. He holds a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery degree from the University of Cape Coast and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Gold Coast. His involvement in NDC politics began during his student days at UCC, where he served as Communications Officer and subsequently President of the university’s TEIN branch. He also became the first medical student at UCC to contest the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) presidency. His political communication work earned him a place on the NDC National Communications Team, where he worked under the leadership of Sammy Gyamfi and benefited from the mentorship of experienced communicators, including Felix Kwakye Ofosu. During the 2024 general election campaign, he served as the party’s Manifesto Spokesperson on Youth Development. Dr Ayeh has also served on the boards of BOST Energies and Ghana Post. He formally entered the race on October 21, 2026, when he picked up nomination forms to contest the Deputy National Communications Officer position. Announcing his bid, he outlined three key priorities: strengthening research-driven political communication, empowering grassroots communicators and improving the party’s strategic media engagement. He said his intention was to build on the existing foundations of the party’s communications machinery and make its messaging more responsive to the aspirations of Ghanaians.

items.title: Deuil à la Chefferie de Canton de Bobo-Dioulasso : Disparition de Sanou Ali dit « Lewi », fils du Chef suprême Bôbô-Mandarê
items.description: La ville de Sya et l'ensemble de la communauté coutumière de Bobo-Dioulasso sont plongées dans une profonde affliction à la suite du décès de Sanou Ali, communément appelé « Lewi ». Fils de Sa Majesté le Chef suprême, Chef de Canton des Bôbô-Mandarê, le défunt s'est éteint le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso des suites d'une courte maladie. L'annonce de sa disparition a suscité une vive vague d'émotion au sein des grandes familles alliées et de la population riveraine, alors que l'inhumation est prévue ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026 au cimetière situé sur la route de Banankélédaga. C'est une triste nouvelle qui secoue la ville de Sya et la Chefferie coutumière. Le samedi 21 novembre 2026, Sanou Ali, affectueusement surnommé « Lewi » par ses proches et connaissances, a rendu son dernier souffle à Bobo-Dioulasso des suites d'une courte maladie. En sa qualité de fils de Sa Majesté le Chef suprême, Chef de Canton des Bôbô-Mandarê, sa disparition endeuille l'une des institutions coutumières les plus emblématiques de la région. Dès l'annonce de la triste nouvelle, l'émotion et la solidarité se sont manifestées autour de la famille éprouvée. Dans un communiqué nécrologique officiel, la Grande Famille de la Chefferie de Canton de Bobo-Dioulasso, la Chefferie suprême Bôbô-Mandarê ainsi que l'ensemble des grandes familles alliées de Sya ont exprimé leur profonde douleur et leur immense tristesse face à cette perte. Elles ont invité les parents, amis et personnes de bonne volonté à s'unir dans le recueillement et la prière pour accompagner le défunt dans son dernier voyage. Le programme des obsèques de Sanou Ali a été officiellement communiqué par la famille royale. L'inhumation est fixée à ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à partir de 11 heures au cimetière situé sur la route de Banankélédaga à Bobo-Dioulasso. En adressant ses condoléances les plus sincères à Sa Majesté, à la famille royale et aux proches, la Chefferie de Canton a imploré la miséricorde divine pour le repos de son âme, souhaitant que la terre libre de Sya lui soit légère. items.title: Argentina midfielder Paredes collapses during TV interview
items.description: World Cup-winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors. The former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder, 32, was suffering from the heat and humidity in Barranquilla, Colombia, where Boca won the Copa Sudamericana by beating Atletico Mineiro of Brazil 2-0. He was replaced in the second half, then collapsed during a television interview, with pictures showing a journalist trying to break his fall. After treatment, Argentine Paredes was able to walk to the dressing room and join his team’s celebrations. “Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness,” he said on Instagram after the match. Heat was a discussion before the game, with forecasts predicting temperatures could reach 32C and humidity around 80%. Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he noticed the midfielder struggling in the second half. “He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half,” Arruabarrena said. “He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling.” Paredes started his career with Boca before moving to Europe in 2015. The victory for Boca ended an 18-year international trophy drought for the Argentine side. By securing their 19th international cup, Boca also became South America’s most decorated club since 1960, overtaking domestic rival Independiente, which has 18.
