items.title: Kozah / session d’assises 2026 : Quatre accuses condamnés à 15 ans de réclusion criminelle et deux autres a 30 ans pour enlèvement et séquestration
items.description: Kara, 22 nov. (ATOP) – Quatre accusés ont été condamnés chacun à 15 ans de réclusion criminelle pour enlèvement, séquestration, extorsion, association de malfaiteurs et détention illégale d’armes à feu, à l’issue d’une audience tenue le samedi 21 novembre à la cour d’appel de Kara. Deux autres, jugés par contumace, ont écopé chacun de 30 ans de réclusion criminelle, tandis qu’un septième accusé a été acquitté et remis en liberté. Les condamnés à 15 ans de réclusion criminelle sont Demo Omarou, alias Dogo, de nationalité béninoise, ainsi que Ousmane Omarou Rouga, Abdoulaye Aboubacar Goda et Ali Nagoli, tous de nationalité nigériane. Les deux autres mis en cause, identifiés sous les noms de Dandjima et Modiane, actuellement en fuite, ont été condamnés chacun à 30 ans de réclusion criminelle. En revanche, Bèlè Mohamadou Babouga, de nationalité nigériane, a été acquitté des faits de complicité qui lui étaient reprochés. Les faits remontent à la nuit du 11 au 12 mars 2019. Aux environs de minuit, cinq individus cagoulés ont fait irruption au campement de Garba Omarou, éleveur et demeurant à Bago (P/Tchamba), dans le village de Kériadè, (P/Sotouboua). Après avoir tiré un coup de fusil en l’air pour dissuader toute intervention, ils ont ligoté le propriétaire des lieux avant de l’emmener dans la brousse. La victime a été séquestrée pendant deux jours dans un endroit inconnu, où elle aurait subi des actes de torture et de barbarie. Ses ravisseurs lui réclamaient cinq millions de FCFA en échange de sa libération, tout en menaçant de la tuer si cette exigence n’était pas satisfaite. À l’aide du téléphone portable de leur otage, ils ont ensuite contacté son jeune frère, Garba Aliou, pour lui réclamer la rançon. À l’issue des négociations, ce dernier a proposé la somme de 2,5 millions de FCFA, acceptée par les ravisseurs à titre d’acompte, avec l’engagement de verser ultérieurement le reliquat. Après avoir réuni le montant convenu, Garba Aliou a été orienté vers un endroit dans la brousse pour y déposer l’argent. La victime a été libérée après que les ravisseurs eurent récupéré les fonds. Conduite à l’hôpital de Sotouboua pour des soins, elle s’est ensuite présentée à la brigade territoriale de gendarmerie d’Adjengré pour porter plainte, ouvrant ainsi la voie à une enquête. À la barre, les accusés ont reconnu les faits qui leur étaient reprochés, à l’exception de Bèlè Mohamadou Babouga, qui a soutenu que les actes incriminés étaient antérieurs à son arrivée dans le milieu. Dans ses réquisitions, le représentant du ministère public, Me Fougou Kpaguidja, s’est appuyé sur les éléments relatifs à la culpabilité et à l’imputabilité des faits aux accusés. Il a également pris en compte les circonstances atténuantes évoquées par les articles 36 à 39 du nouveau code pénal (NCP) ainsi que la nécessité de prononcer des peines complémentaires. Il a requis 30 ans de réclusion criminelle contre chacun des accusés. De leur côté, Me N’Djellé Abby Edah et son collaborateur, Me Abi Essodog, conseils de Bèlè Mohamadou et d’Ousmane Omarou Rouga, ont plaidé l’acquittement de leurs clients. Pour le premier, la défense a notamment mis en avant la chronologie des faits, soulignant qu’il n’était revenu au pays que le 17 mars 2019, soit après les événements des 11 et 12 mars, et qu’il avait été interpellé six jours plus tard. Concernant Ousmane Omarou Rouga, elle a estimé qu’aucune preuve matérielle au dossier ne permettait d’établir son intention criminelle ni sa participation active aux faits. Les avocats ont, par ailleurs, invité la cour à écarter toute responsabilité fondée sur une simple association avec les autres accusés. Pour sa part, Me Gbéleou Koumoyi, avocat de Demo Omarou alias Dogo, Abdoulaye Aboubacar Goda et Ali Nagoli, a contesté la sévérité des réquisitions du ministère public. Il a plaidé la prise en compte de circonstances atténuantes et sollicité la clémence de la cour. Au terme de 13 heures de débats, la cour a reconnu Demo Omarou alias Dogo, Ousmane Omarou Rouga, Abdoulaye Aboubacar Goda et Ali Nagoli coupables des faits retenus contre eux, avec bénéfice de circonstances atténuantes. Ils ont été condamnés chacun à 15 ans de réclusion criminelle, assortis d’une interdiction du territoire togolais de 20 ans et d’une expulsion à l’issue de leur peine. Les deux accusés en fuite, Dandjima et Modiane, ont été reconnus coupables sans bénéfice de circonstances atténuantes et condamnés chacun à 30 ans de réclusion criminelle. Un mandat d’arrêt a été délivré à leur encontre. Les faits reprochés aux prévenus sont prévus et punis par les dispositions des articles 47, 49, 50, 51, 283, 286 alinéas 1er et 2, 463 alinéas 4, 465 alinéa 1er ainsi que 549 du nouveau Code pénal et décret n° 95-11/PR du 19 avril 1995 réglementant les armes et munitions. Bèlè Mohamadou Babouga a, quant à lui, été acquitté des faits de complicité et a recouvré sa liberté. ATOP/SG/TAL/MD

items.title: FIFM : Hommage à John Turturro, un acteur libre au service d’un cinéma sans frontières
items.description: Le Festival international du film de Marrakech a célébré John Turturro, dimanche soir, en lui décernant son Étoile d’Or. Présenté par l’actrice Golshifteh Farahani, l’acteur, scénariste et réalisateur américain a reçu cette distinction avec émotion, évoquant ses débuts, les rencontres qui ont jalonné sa carrière et cette volonté de rester, malgré les décennies, un « débutant » toujours prêt à se réinventer. Après plusieurs décennies au service du cinéma, John Turturro a été célébré dimanche soir au Festival international du film de Marrakech. L’acteur, scénariste et réalisateur américain a reçu l’Étoile d’Or du FIFM, une distinction accueillie avec beaucoup d’humilité par celui qui revendique encore aujourd’hui une forme de curiosité et de disponibilité propres aux débuts d’une carrière. Pour lui rendre hommage, le festival a choisi Golshifteh Farahani, dont le parcours résonne avec certains des thèmes qui traversent l’œuvre de Turturro. Prenant la parole devant le public marrakchi, l’actrice a d’abord évoqué son propre lien avec le Maroc. C’est dans le Royaume, il y a près de vingt ans, qu’elle a tourné son premier film hollywoodien, « Body of Lies », à Rabat et à Ouarzazate. Une expérience qui, a-t-elle expliqué, a contribué à changer le cours de sa vie. Mounir Mehimdate « Après avoir été si déracinée, il n’y a aucun autre endroit où l’on peut véritablement trouver refuge, si ce n’est dans l’amour, dans l’art, et bien sûr dans le cinéma » , a-t-elle confié, avant de relier cette expérience à la famille cinématographique réunie à Marrakech. « Avec John, le corps devient un langage » C’est dans ce registre que Golshifteh Farahani a ensuite dressé le portrait de John Turturro. Elle a salué un « artiste engagé », pour qui la liberté du corps et celle du jeu occupent une place centrale. « Une silhouette, un regard, une présence légèrement décalée, une énergie nerveuse dans chaque geste » , a-t-elle décrit, estimant qu’avec Turturro, « le corps devient un langage ». L’actrice a également rappelé la richesse d’une filmographie construite à travers des univers très différents. Des frères Coen à Spike Lee, Turturro a incarné des personnages devenus emblématiques, de Barton Fink à Jesus Quintana dans The Big Lebowski, en passant notamment par Do the Right Thing et Jungle Fever. Mounir Mehimdate Pour Farahani, cette capacité à passer du rire au désespoir, du cri au murmure, sans perdre la vérité de ses personnages constitue précisément la marque des plus grands acteurs. Mais son hommage est également devenu plus intime. Elle a souligné la manière dont Turturro a souvent donné vie à des personnages « déracinés » , « en marge » ou encore à ceux qui cherchent leur place dans le monde. « Tu sais ce que nous portons en nous lorsque notre histoire commence ailleurs, et je sais ce que nous portons lorsque nous avons dû partir » , lui a-t-elle lancé, établissant un parallèle avec sa propre histoire d’exil. Pour elle, le cinéma de Turturro dépasse ainsi les frontières : « C’est la liberté de tous les possibles : se comprendre les uns les autres, s’ouvrir aux autres, parler et partager. » Turturro : « Je me considère toujours comme un débutant » Visiblement ému par cet hommage, John Turturro a à son tour pris la parole pour remercier les organisateurs du festival, le prince Moulay Rachid et l’ensemble du public marocain. L’acteur a surtout choisi de revenir sur ce que représente, pour lui, le métier de comédien. « Je suis une personne très chanceuse de bien gagner ma vie en tant qu'acteur, et parfois en tant que scénariste et réalisateur, en faisant quelque chose que j'aime profondément », a-t-il déclaré. Une conception du travail héritée de ses parents, auxquels il attribue une conviction simple : « Un travail bien fait définit qui vous êtes. » Mounir Mehimdate Turturro a ensuite comparé la construction d’une carrière artistique à celle d’une maison ou d’un vêtement, qui prennent forme « brique par brique, point par point ». Une manière de rappeler que le cinéma, comme toute œuvre, se construit dans le temps, à travers les rencontres et les contributions de chacun. L’acteur a également cité l’écrivain italien Cesare Pavese, selon lequel « la seule grande chose dans la vie est de commencer ». Une phrase qui semble particulièrement lui correspondre. « Je me considère toujours comme un débutant à bien des égards », a-t-il confié. Pour lui, chaque nouveau projet possède la fraîcheur d’un premier engagement : « Chaque projet est comme un premier amour. » Une Étoile d’Or comme encouragement à continuer Plutôt que de considérer son prix comme l’aboutissement d’une carrière, John Turturro l’a présenté comme une invitation à poursuivre son chemin. « Je considère cette récompense comme un encouragement à continuer d’essayer » , a-t-il conclu. À Marrakech, l’hommage rendu à John Turturro aura ainsi dépassé la célébration d’une filmographie. Il aura surtout mis en lumière une certaine idée du cinéma : un art fondé sur la liberté, la rencontre, la transmission et la capacité à faire tomber les frontières. Mounir Mehimdate Et derrière la reconnaissance d’un acteur devenu une figure majeure du septième art, c’est peut-être justement l’homme qui refuse de se considérer comme arrivé que le FIFM a choisi de célébrer. The post FIFM : Hommage à John Turturro, un acteur libre au service d’un cinéma sans frontières appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Macabre découverte à Athènes : Une jeune Burkinabè de 24 ans retrouvée dans une valise, le suspect guinéen aux mains de la justice française
items.description: La découverte macabre du corps sans vie d'Aramata, une ressortissante burkinabè de 24 ans dissimulée dans une valise au cœur d'Athènes, choque la diaspora africaine et plonge sa famille au Burkina Faso dans un profond désarroi. Portée disparue fin octobre 2026, la jeune femme aurait été tuée au domicile d'un ressortissant guinéen de 19 ans. Grâce à une étroite coopération policière internationale et à la délivrance d'un mandat d'arrêt européen, le principal suspect a été interpellé à Strasbourg le 18 novembre dernier. Alors que les procédures d'extradition s'organisent et que l'Organisation des femmes africaines en Grèce dénonce un féminicide, les proches de la victime supplient les autorités et les bonnes volontés de soutenir le rapatriement de sa dépouille. L'horreur a frappé le centre de la capitale grecque au début du mois de novembre. Le 8 novembre 2026, un passant intrigué par une odeur nauséabonde s'échappant d'une valise abandonnée rue Alkamenous, près de la place Victoria dans le quartier d'Agios Panteleimonas, a immédiatement prévenu les forces de l'ordre. Sur place, les policiers ont découvert le corps en décomposition d'une jeune femme, les jambes entravées par une corde. L'analyse ADN et les empreintes ont confirmé qu'il s'agissait d'Aramata, une jeune ressortissante du Burkina Faso âgée de 24 ans, dont la disparition avait été signalée le 29 octobre par une amie. Avant son retour à Athènes fin octobre, la jeune femme avait travaillé dans le secteur hôtelier sur l'île de Folégandros. Les enquêteurs de la brigade criminelle ont rapidement reconstitué son parcours : les caméras de vidéo-surveillance l'ont montrée entrant dans un immeuble le 29 octobre avec un jeune Guinéen de 19 ans. Si la jeune femme n'est jamais ressortie vivante du logement, le suspect a été filmé quelques jours plus tard, transportant une imposante valise qu'il a déposée dans la rue. La fuite du présumé meurtrier aura été de courte durée face au déploiement de la coopération policière européenne. Selon les investigations, le suspect aurait conservé le corps plusieurs jours dans sa chambre avant de le déposer à l'extérieur, puis de s'envoler le 9 novembre vers la France. Avant son départ, il aurait avoué les faits à son colocataire, surpris par la forte odeur régnant dans le logement. Saisies du dossier, les autorités judiciaires grecques ont immédiatement émis un mandat d'arrêt européen. Localisé par les services de police français, le jeune homme de 19 ans a été interpellé le 18 novembre 2026 à Strasbourg. Il fait actuellement l'objet d'une procédure d'extradition vers la Grèce, où le médecin légiste devra établir avec certitude les causes exactes du décès, l'asphyxie ou la surdose n'étant pas exclues. Au-delà du volet judiciaire, ce drame suscite un vif émoi et ravive le débat sur la vulnérabilité des femmes migrantes. L'Organisation des femmes africaines en Grèce a fermement dénoncé un féminicide, soulignant que cette tragédie met en lumière la précarité, l'isolement et la précarité économique auxquelles sont confrontées de nombreuses femmes en situation d'exil. Au Burkina Faso, la nouvelle a provoqué un choc immense au sein de la famille d'Aramata : son père a dû être hospitalisé en urgence, tandis que sa mère a lancé un appel vibrant à la solidarité et à l'appui des autorités pour permettre le rapatriement du corps de sa fille vers sa terre natale. items.title: PSG’s Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL
items.description: Paris Saint-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. The 21-year-old was in tears as he was carried off on a stretcher toward the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions’ 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday night . Doue, arguably PSG’s best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down with no contact. The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue, visibly in pain, received treatment before the crowd applauded him off at the Allianz Riviera Stadium. It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries. The European champions have been plagued by injuries so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury against Barcelona in October. PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

items.title: ‎Burkina : Dr Guilga François de Paule Yambressinga plaide pour le remplacement des délégations spéciales par des conseils révolutionnaires municipaux
items.description: ‎Dans cette tribune rendue publique, Dr Guilga François de Paule Yambressinga, Docteur en histoire économique et sociale contemporaine, spécialiste en gouvernance territoriale, management des entreprises et des organisations plaide pour une réforme de la gouvernance locale au Burkina Faso. Il préconise le remplacement des délégations spéciales par des Conseils révolutionnaires municipaux (CRM). Selon lui, maintenues depuis 2022 à la tête des communes, les délégations spéciales montrent des limites, notamment leur tendance à privilégier la gestion des affaires courantes au détriment des investissements structurants et des initiatives de développement local. ‎Il évoque également un décalage entre le fonctionnement actuel de ces instances et les nouvelles dispositions réglementaires issues du décret du 16 mars 2026. Il estime que la dynamique de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) doit également se traduire dans la gouvernance des collectivités territoriales. Guilga François de Paule YAMBRESSINGA Docteur en histoire économique et sociale contemporaine, spécialiste en gouvernance territoriale, management des entreprises et des organisations Tél : (00226) 76 65 42 16 - Email : yambre78@gmail.com Depuis l'année 2022, l'ensemble des communes burkinabè est placé sous l'administration d'une délégation spéciale. Le recours à cette instance comme organe de gouvernance locale n'est pas une nouveauté. Cette pratique a marqué l'histoire du processus de communalisation au Burkina Faso. La première délégation spéciale a été instituée en 1959, avant la proclamation de l'indépendance du pays. Après l'accession à l'autonomie, le contexte politique national et local (insurrections populaires, révolutions, transition politique, dysfonctionnements des assemblées locales,) a conduit à la pérennisation de la délégation spéciale en tant qu'instance délibérante des communes. (G.F. Yambressinga, 2025, p.59). En fonction des impératifs d'administration de chaque régime politique, voire de chaque époque, la nature, la composition et le fonctionnement de la délégation spéciale ont constamment varié. En effet, selon le décret n°2022-0118 /PRES-TRANS/PM/MATDS/MEFP du 03 mai 2022 portant conditions d'installation, composition, organisation, attributions et fonctionnement de délégations spéciales, la délégation spéciale est une commission administrative composée de membres nommés par le gouvernement dans une collectivité territoriale pour assurer l'administration de la collectivité, lorsque l'organe délibérant a été dissout, lorsqu'il ne peut se réunir du fait de la démission de ses membres ou à la suite de l'annulation définitive de l'élection de l'ensemble de ses membres (Décret n°2022-0118, article 2). Dans la même veine, le décret n°2026-0279/PF/PRIM/MATM/MEF du 16 mars 2026 portant composition et modalités d'installation des délégations spéciales en son article 2, définit la délégation spéciale comme « une assemblée locale composée de membres nommés pour administrer la commune de moyen exercice. Elle est mise en place de façon exceptionnelle pour administrer une région, une commue à statut particulier, une commune de plein exercice et un arrondissement ». Ce décret qui découle de la loi n° 024-2025/ALT du 30 septembre 2025 portant code général des collectivités territoriales a abrogé en son article 36 le décret n°2022-0118 /PRES-TRANS/PM/MATDS/MEFP portant conditions d'installation, composition, organisation, attributions et fonctionnement de délégations spéciales. Mais, force est de constater que la composition et le fonctionnement des délégations spéciales actuelles continuent de s'appuyer sur les dispositions du décret du 3 mai 2022, alors même que celui-ci a été officiellement abrogé. Les communes restent entre les mains de délégations spéciales dont la composition et le fonctionnement ne sont pas en phase non seulement avec le nouveau règlement en vigueur mais surtout avec la dynamique révolutionnaire dans laquelle le pays s'est engagé. Le changement qui s'est opéré dans la gouvernance du pays avec l'avènement de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP) ne doit pas être l'affaire du seul État central mais de celle des deux sphères de la gouvernance à savoir l'État et les communes. Il convient que les communes se dotent d'organes de gouvernance révolutionnaires en lieu et place des délégations spéciales pour être en phase avec la dynamique enclenchée au sommet de l'Etat. La délégation spéciale actuelle est d'ailleurs une commission administrative qui a été instituée en 2022 comme un organe transitoire, mis en place pour gérer les communes et les régions dans le contexte de la transition politique instaurée par la Charte de la transition du 1er mars 2022. Organe temporaire installé pour gérer les affaires courantes, la délégation spéciale tombe dans l'immobilisme lorsqu'elle devient permanente. Du fait de la prudence administrative et de l'application du principe de précaution, la délégation spéciale a tendance à maintenir l'existant. Elle se contente le plus souvent d'assurer le fonctionnement de l'administration locale. C'est une approche de gestion des affaires courantes qui est privilégiée. On ne s'engage pas dans les investissements structurants qui sont toujours reportés faute aussi de ressources (B. L. Somé, 2023, p. 73). Par exemple, les aménagements fonciers tels que les lotissements et les restructurations sont mis en veilleuse. Ces interventions nécessitent d'importantes ressources financières, mais suscitent surtout des remous sociaux. Des présidents de délégations spéciales, par mesure de prudence, se réservent d'engager ces aménagements. Pour rompre avec cette routine, le décret du 16 mars 2026 a transformé les commissions administratives en assemblées locales plus inclusives (prise en compte des personnes handicapées et des forces vives de la collectivité) pour apporter des innovations dans la gouvernance locale. Mais en attendant l'application de ce décret, la gouvernance actuelle des collectivités appelle une profonde refondation afin de s'inscrire pleinement dans la dynamique de la RPP. Alors faudrait-il mettre en place des instances révolutionnaires à la tête des communes à l'image des Conseils révolutionnaires municipaux (CRM) mis en place sous la Révolution démocratique et populaire (RDP). Le CRM a été institué en 1983 par le décret n°83-266 CNR/PRES/IS du 23 décembre 1983. Sa mise en place s'inscrivait dans la volonté du Conseil national de la Révolution de révolutionner la gouvernance locale en remplaçant les mécanismes classiques de gestion municipale une organisation inspirée des principes de la RDP. La gestion des communes fut ainsi confiée aux CRM qui étaient des assemblées populaires regroupant les Comités de Défense de la Révolution (CDR) des différents secteurs communaux (Ordonnance n° 83-21/CNR/PRES, Art.57). L'objectif visé était de rapprocher les instances décisionnelles des populations afin qu'elles participent à la gestion de leur cadre de vie, de leur cité. Ses attributions étaient entre autres l'adoption du budget communal, la délibération sur toutes les questions de gestion municipale, la contribution à la mise en œuvre des orientations politiques et sociales de la Révolution. Le CRM élisait en son sein, les membres de son bureau appelé bureau de coordination communale qui, en tant qu'organe exécutif, était chargé de la coordination et de la mise en œuvre des décisions du CRM (S. Jaglin, 1995, p.82). Le CRM a réussi à enclencher la participation des populations aux initiatives de développement local. Celles-ci ont contribué physiquement à la réalisation d'infrastructures éducatives sanitaires, à des travaux d'aménagement, d'assainissement et d'embellissement des villes. En associant ainsi les populations à la réalisation des infrastructures communautaires, le CRM a contribué à développer une citoyenneté active, une culture de responsabilité collective dans la gestion des affaires locales. Il a été une expérience sans précédent de mobilisation sociale pour l'intérêt général et un mode inédit de représentation locale reposant sur les structures populaires géographiques plutôt que sur les mécanismes classiques de représentation politique. S'inspirer de cette expérience de la RDP en installant des CRM à la tête des communes permet de porter la RPP au niveau local pour instaurer une gouvernance révolutionnaire à la base et de sortir de nombreuses communes de la léthargie dans laquelle elles se sont installées sous l'administration des délégations spéciales. Références bibliographiques Loi n° 024-2025/ALT du 30 septembre 2025 portant code général des collectivités territoriales Loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre2004 portant Code général des collectivités territoriales Ordonnance n° 83-21/CNR/PRES du 14 novembre 1983, relative à l'organisation administrative du territoire. Décret n°2026-0279/PF/PRIM/MATM/MEF du 16 mars 2026 portant composition et modalités d'installation des délégations spéciales. Décret n°2022-004/PRES/MPSR du 1er février 2022 portant dissolution des Conseils de collectivités territoriales. Décret n°2022-0118 /PRES-TRANS/PM/MATDS/MEFP du 03 mai 2022 portant conditions d'installation, composition, organisation, attributions et fonctionnement de délégations spéciales. items.title: Traitement des maladies non transmissibles : Des professionnels de la santé des USP d’Assoli outillés
items.description: Bafilo, 22 nov. (ATOP) – Des professionnels de la santé des Unités de soins périphériques (USP) d’Assoli, ont suivi une formation sur les méthodes de prise en charge adéquate des maladies non transmissibles, à Assoli, les 20 et 21 novembre, à Bafilo. Cette formation est organisée par l’Association programme d’action pour le développement durable (PA2D) au Togo, en collaboration avec ses partenaires venus de la Belgique. Axée sur les thématiques du diabète, de l’hypertension artérielle et de l’hygiène publique, la formation a été riche en échanges d’expériences entre les professionnels de santé de la Belgique et ceux d’Assoli. Ils ont partagé les méthodes pratiquées en Belgique et celles pratiquées au Togo, à Assoli. Ces échanges ont permis d’outiller les professionnels de santé d’Assoli en méthodes de prise en charge adéquate des maladies non transmissibles. Les partenaires ont également mis à leur disposition des kits qui leur permettront de dépister ces maladies dès le début de leur phase. Ces kits comprennent notamment des tensiomètres, des glycomètres et des lunettes solaires. Le secrétaire général de l’association PA2D, Bah Sani Zikiroulloh, a expliqué qu’aujourd’hui, les questions liées au diabète et à la tension artérielle sont inquiétantes, car ces maladies non transmissibles se soignent à des coûts élevés. Les personnes atteintes de ces maladies, dit-il, n’ont pas les moyens de se faire soigner, d’où la nécessité d’organiser cette formation pour outiller les prestataires de soins afin que les populations ne se retrouvent pas à des phases avancées. « La prise en charge à la phase avancée n’est pas facile en raison de son coût très élevé. C’est la raison qui a motivé la rencontre », a-t-il indiqué. Les bénéficiaires de la formation ont exprimé leur satisfaction. Pour l’infirmier auxiliaire d’État, Alassani Moufoutaou, venu de l’USP de Koumondè, cette formation a comblé ses attentes. « Je suis très satisfait de la formation. Je promets de restituer fidèlement ces acquis à mes camarades qui n’ont pas pu participer, pour que nous puissions ensemble améliorer nos prestations », a-t-il martelé. ATOP/GMM/MD

items.title: Pochettino endures nightmare start as Man United lose to Liverpool
items.description: Mauricio Pochettino’s reign as Manchester United head coach began in desperate fashion, as his team were thrashed by rivals Liverpool and remained in the Premier League relegation zone. Almost everything that could go wrong for the visitors did in the first 13 minutes: they conceded two goals and had Leny Yoro sent off, and Liverpool cruised to victory from there. This was the first time since 1937 that the Red Devils arrived at Anfield in the bottom three, and back then they lost to Liverpool in a season that ended in relegation. It seems unthinkable for the present-day Manchester United to suffer a similar fate, but this performance and result underlined the size of the task facing Pochettino as he looks to drag them up the table. Yoro received a straight red card in the eighth minute after he was adjudged to have fouled Alexander Isak just outside the box. Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to send the free-kick into the bottom left corner. It got worse for the visitors when Liverpool – looking capable of scoring with every attack – added a second. This time, Rio Ngumoha got a cross in from the left and Florian Wirtz produced a clever volley at an awkward angle. The only positive for the visitors in the first half was that they conceded no further goals, but they were left with a mountain to climb. Liverpool fans may have thought a repeat of their 7-0 win over Manchester United three and a half years ago was on the cards, but the hosts seemed to step off their attack in the second half. The longer it went without a third goal, some Manchester United fans may have hoped for a comeback, but any such thoughts were banished when Ngumoha slotted in from Bradley Barcola’s pass. That goal prompted taunts of “going down” from Liverpool fans, and United fans had more pain to come as the hosts added a fourth late on, with Victor Munoz firing home from Florian Wirtz’s neat ball behind the defence. The performance and result will give Pochettino plenty to ponder over as it leaves Manchester United just one point off the foot of the table. Liverpool, meanwhile, are fourth. Liverpool analysis: Wirtz stars as Reds take their chances Liverpool look to be taking encouraging steps under Andoni Iraola, with just two losses in 11 Premier League games so far. But most of their joy has come away from home, with four wins from their five league road trips. Home form needed to improve as they went into Sunday’s game, having won just once in the Premier League before Manchester United’s arrival. One issue for the Reds has been turning chances into goals, a problem highlighted at the start of November in a home defeat by Arsenal, when they had 17 efforts at goal but none on target. Undoubtedly, the early red card helped Liverpool here, but they took their chances early to keep this from becoming a frustrating battle against a side looking to nullify the player disadvantage by defending deep. Wirtz’s acrobatic finish was crucial, and the German midfielder rounded off a fine game with the assist for Liverpool’s fourth. After a slow start, he looks more like the player the Reds believed they were getting when they signed him last year. Man Utd analysis: Size of task made clear for Pochettino Even the most optimistic Manchester United fan knew a change of leader wouldn’t instantly fix their problems. That said, they would have reasonably expected the new-boss bounce to last longer than eight minutes. Hope filled the away end as they welcomed yet another new era, and former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino was certainly not afraid to make bold decisions immediately, handing Matthijs de Ligt his first start of the year. But all the pre-match planning was hugely disrupted when Yoro was sent off for the second time this season. Pochettino will have to work on discipline, with this being Manchester United’s third red card in four games. It is part of the wider issue of the Red Devils’ dreadful defending. The four goals they conceded in this game mean they have let in 34 in all competitions this season, more than any other side from Europe’s top five leagues. For now, they remain in an almost unthinkable position – second bottom of the Premier League and facing the very real possibility of a season-long mission to avoid relegation.

items.title: Wawa/Le chef du canton de Kessibo a reçu son décret de reconnaissance
items.description: Badou, 20 nov. (ATOP) – Investi de la légitimité coutumière et désormais revêtu de la consécration étatique, Oluķè Edzi Yawo Abuewudza Ihou VI, chef du canton de Kessibo, commune Wawa 1, a reçu, le vendredi 20 novembre dans la localité, son décret portant reconnaissance officielle, de chef traditionnel dudit canton. La cérémonie a été présidée par le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, le général de brigade Dadja Maganawè. Celui-ci avait à ses côtés le nouveau préfet de Wawa, Djimbondjo Bintiene Laré, des parlementaires, des conseillers municipaux et régionaux, ainsi qu’un parterre de têtes couronnées venues de la préfecture et des contrées limitrophes. Le gouverneur, Gal Dadja Maganawè a circonscrit les hautes responsabilités qui s’attachent désormais à la charge du nouveau dignitaire. Il a rappelé que l’institution traditionnelle demeure un pilier indispensable pour préserver la cohésion sociale, perpétuer les savoir-être, savoir-faire et savoir-vivre, hérités des ancêtres, et consolider la paix ainsi que la stabilité. L’autorité régionale a mis en exergue l’exigence de sagesse, d’intégrité et d’abnégation qu’impose l’exercice du pouvoir coutumier. « Vous êtes le gardien des us et coutumes. Vous devez veiller à l’harmonie et à la cohésion sociale à travers l’arbitrage et la conciliation des parties en matière coutumière, être digne et loyal envers les autorités locales et l’État », a martelé le général de brigade Dadja Maganawè. Le récipiendaire, Oluķè Edzi Yawo Abuewudza Ihou VI, a salué l’action du président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, en faveur de la valorisation et de la consolidation de la chefferie traditionnelle au Togo. Il s’est engagé à observer avec rigueur les directives de l’autorité régionale, à œuvrer loyalement au service des intérêts supérieurs de la nation et à promouvoir l’épanouissement socio-économique de ses administrés. Sa majesté Ihou VI a invité les habitants de Kessibo à lui accorder leur concours et leur adhésion, afin d’impulser un essor équilibré et pérenne du canton. ATOP/PM/KKT/KYA

items.title: Ghana Institute of Architects proposes structured partnership to protect Ghana’s architectural heritage
items.description: The Ghana Institute of Architects (GIA) has proposed the introduction of a legislative instrument to strengthen the protection and preservation of Ghana’s architectural heritage as part of efforts to position architecture as a key driver of tourism and socioeconomic development. The proposal includes a review of existing policies and the introduction of new legislation to establish a structured partnership between government, architects and other stakeholders in the built environment. The proposal was made at the GIA’s 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM), held in Ho, Volta Region, under the theme, “Architecture as a Catalyst for Tourism in Ghana.” Addressing the opening ceremony, GIA President, Tony Asare called for deliberate efforts to preserve the country’s architectural heritage, particularly historic buildings and structures, while harnessing their potential to attract tourists and stimulate economic growth. He stressed the need for architects to play a central role in national development, particularly in town planning, urban design and infrastructure development. Mr Asare proposed that all Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) engage qualified architects in managing planning and development processes. He further advocated that major public infrastructure projects, including airports, transport terminals, cultural centres, museums, waterfronts, parks and markets, should be designed under the leadership of qualified architects. National programme for heritage conservation The GIA President also called for a national programme to guide the conservation, adaptive reuse and interpretation of Ghana’s built heritage. He said the programme should establish design standards for tourism corridors, town gateways, rest stops, signage and public amenities. Mr Asare proposed pilot projects in selected tourism destinations, beginning in the Volta Region, to demonstrate how quality architectural design could enhance the attractiveness and functionality of Ghanaian communities. He emphasised that a shared national vision was needed to position architecture at the centre of tourism development, job creation, cultural preservation and sustainable development. “Ghana’s next great tourism asset will not emerge by chance. It must be designed, built, and protected by Ghanaians,” he said. Malta proposes architectural exchange programme The Malta High Commissioner to Ghana, His Excellency Ronald Micallef, highlighted how Malta has leveraged its architectural heritage to promote tourism and stimulate economic growth. He proposed an architectural exchange programme between the Ghana Institute of Architects and a counterpart institution in Malta to facilitate knowledge-sharing and strengthen professional development. Mr Micallef also encouraged Ghanaian architects to embrace climate-responsive architecture by incorporating features such as natural ventilation, shading and water conservation into building designs. Government commits resources to tourism infrastructure The Minister for Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, said the government was investing in road infrastructure to improve access to tourism destinations across the country. He disclosed that GH¢30 billion had been committed to the Big Push initiative to improve selected roads, with an additional GH¢10 billion allocated to the road sector in 2027. According to him, the government was working closely with the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts to improve road networks serving tourism destinations. He noted that the journey to a tourist destination should itself form part of the visitor experience, stressing the importance of incorporating architectural expertise into infrastructure development. Mr Agbodza also disclosed that the government had allocated US$1 billion to the tourism sector under the New Economy initiative. He described tourism as the fifth pillar of the initiative and urged architects to collaborate with the Ministry of Tourism to identify innovative ways of unlocking the sector’s potential. Tourism Minister pledges collaboration with GIA The Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Dzifa Abla Gomashie, pledged her ministry’s commitment to working with the Ghana Institute of Architects to strengthen the country’s tourism industry. She expressed concern about encroachment on buffer zones around heritage sites, warning that uncontrolled development and other human activities were threatening historic buildings and their surrounding environments. “I am looking forward to deepening our partnership with the Ghana Institute of Architects in several important areas,” she said. Her remarks highlighted the need for stronger collaboration between government and professional institutions to safeguard heritage sites while promoting sustainable tourism development. Volta Regional Minister highlights architects’ role in nation-building The Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, also acknowledged the significant contribution of architects to national development. He described architects as nation-builders whose expertise was essential to shaping the country’s infrastructure, communities and economic future. He called for stronger collaboration between the government and the architectural profession to advance Ghana’s development agenda. The discussions at the AGM reinforced the importance of integrating architectural expertise into national planning and tourism development, while protecting historic structures and promoting sustainable design. The proposed legislative instrument, if pursued, could provide an important framework for strengthening heritage conservation, improving the quality of public infrastructure and ensuring that Ghana’s architectural identity remains an integral part of its tourism appeal.

items.title: Alcaraz outplays Zverev for first ATP Finals triumph
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz outplayed world number one Alexander Zverev to end his wait for his first ATP Finals title and complete a remarkable post-injury return. A season which began with Alcaraz becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, before he was ruled out for more than four months with a wrist issue, ended with the Spaniard holding aloft another of the sport’s biggest trophies. Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break. It was a statement win over Zverev, who took advantage of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner’s injury absences to top the rankings and claim his first two major titles. It was Alcaraz’s 14th successive win and his third straight title triumph, and he proved beyond a doubt that he is back to his devastating best. “Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time; it means the world to me,” the 23-year-old said. “I have been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. For me, it’s been an amazing week. “I couldn’t finish the week in a better way.” Alcaraz ends long wait for ATP Finals glory It’s been just 84 days since Alcaraz returned at the US Open in August after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. Since then, the current world number three has won 21 of his 22 matches and swept titles at four of the five tournaments he’s entered. With his latest victory, Alcaraz has become the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the season-ending Finals – and only the fourth in history. Zverev, who ends 2026 with an ATP Tour-leading 69 match victories, had not dropped serve in four straight-set matches to reach the final. But for much of the two-hour title decider, Alcaraz dismantled his greatest weapon with brilliant tennis. Alcaraz handled the occasion far better, emerging from a tense start with a 4-1 double-break lead as he headed into the first set. Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals for the first time on his fourth appearance at the season-ending tournament The two players’ contrasting emotions were evident when Alcaraz wore a big grin after pulling off a between-the-legs lob that Zverev smashed into the net. At the other end of the court, the German threw away his racquet in disgust. While Alcaraz danced to music during a change of ends, Zverev’s frustration only grew as, after winning back one of the two breaks of serve, he received a second time violation and lost serve for a third straight game. The top seed left the court after unravelling in the first set, producing just three winners and committing 19 unforced errors in an inconsistent start. Alcaraz’s march to the title appeared inevitable as he took control of the second set with a fourth break of serve, but Zverev restored parity in the eighth game and kept his hopes alive by forcing a tie-break. Overcoming a 3-0 tiebreak deficit, Zverev then won six straight points to reach three set points. However, he failed to convert them all, including one on his own serve, before Alcaraz drove in a backhand winner on his second match point. After picking himself up off the floor, the Spaniard celebrated with his team in the stands after finally landing the title he had been chasing for four years. In doubles, French debutants Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti lifted the trophy after a comeback win over Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic. The sixth seeds recovered from a first-set loss to win 3-6 7-6 (7-2) 10-6, ending the year with the most wins (59) and titles (seven) in men’s doubles.

items.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday. After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament. Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals. With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998. “It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament. A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles. But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals. He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one. Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings. – Topsy-turvy – The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three. The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week. Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold. Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand. Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1. Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native’s serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob. A netted backhand by Zverev — his 19th unforced error of the match — on Alcaraz’s first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame. Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance. The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points. But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve. The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand. The post Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Incendie à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives : Des tonnes de marchandises consumées par les flammes
items.description: Le vendredi 20 novembre 2026, le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana est allé constater les dégâts de l’incendie intervenu le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives (ZACA) sise à l’arrondissement 1 de Ouagadougou. La date du jeudi 19 novembre 2026 restera graver dans les mémoires des commerçants de la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives (ZACA) de Ouagadougou. Pour cause, un incendie intervenu aux environs de 19h. A son passage, il a causé d’énormes dégâts matériels. Des marchandises, des motos, des batteries et d’autres matériaux plastique ont été touchées par les flammes. Ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, le ministre de la Securité, Mahamadou Sana est allé constater la situation. « Nous sommes venus aujourd’hui nous s’imprégner de la situation réelle sur le terrain. Nous nous sommes rendus compte qu’il ne s’agissait pas des explosifs mais plutôt des matières dangereuses notamment des insecticides surement mal conditionnés ou qui ont été mis dans des conditions favorisant le déclenchement de cet incendie. Les sapeurs-pompiers ont pu intervenir à temps et on a eu que des dégâts matériels, heureusement pas de dégât humaine » a-t-il constaté. Selon lui, le transport de ces produits obéit à certaines règles, que ce soit des bouteilles de gaz, des insecticides. « Il y a des normes strictes à respecter en matière des transports, et quand on les respecte, il va de soi qu’il ait un meilleur transport mais quand on ne le fait pas, ces genres d’incidents interviennent et le moindre incident va causer d’énorme dégât » a -t-il expliqué. A cet effet, il a invité les transporteurs au respect strict de cette règlementation. Séance tenante, le ministre a donné des instructions à son département pour qu’une campagne de sensibilisation soit menée au profit des populations sur le transport des marchandises et la brigade Laabal est mis à contribution pour le contrôle de transport de certaines marchandises dans les marchés et yaars. Synthèse de Fleur BIRBA Sidwaya L’article Incendie à la zone d’activités commerciales et administratives : Des tonnes de marchandises consumées par les flammes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Two teens arrested for alleged GH¢38,000 romance scam
items.description: The Assin Fosu District Court has remanded two teenagers from Ajumako-Besease into police custody for allegedly defrauding a Bibiani-based miner of GH₵38,477 through a WhatsApp and mobile money romance scam. The suspects, Kweku Mintah, aged 19, and Kelvin Afful, 16, allegedly used a fabricated romantic relationship and a fake motor accident story to convince their victim to send them money. The court did not accept their plea on charges of conspiracy to commit a crime, obtaining payment by electronic means, and theft. However, during Police interrogation, the suspect allegedly claimed to have committed the alleged act and shared the proceeds. The suspects were to reappear in court on Thursday, December 3. Chief Inspector Gilbert Abangna Anyongo, the Prosecutor, told the court presided over Abdul Majid Illiasu that the complainant, Mr Eddie Norman, received a WhatsApp message on July 27, 2026, from Afful, who introduced himself as a woman named Joyce, and the two subsequently developed a friendship through their conversations. During their subsequent conversations, the purported Joyce allegedly asked the miner for transport money to visit him, to which he agreed and sent GH₵500. The Prosecutor said the alleged scheme took another turn when the miner received a disguised call from someone claiming to be Joyce’s grandmother, later identified as Mintah. The Prosecutor said the caller reportedly encouraged the miner to take good care of her granddaughter when she arrived in Bibiani; however, “Joyce” never showed up. Hours later, the supposed grandmother allegedly contacted the miner again, this time claiming that “Joyce” had been involved in a motor accident while travelling to see him and was in critical condition and appealed for urgent financial assistance to cater for her medical needs, the Prosecutor said. Concerned about the alleged accident, the Prosecutor said the miner began sending money whenever demands were made, transferring funds to two numbers registered in the names of Elizabeth Arthur and Anthony Afful. The Police said the miner eventually sent a total of GH₵38,477 before realising that he had allegedly fallen victim to a scam and subsequently reported the matter to the Central North Regional Police Cyber Crime Unit for assistance. Police investigations led to an application for a disclosure order from the Assin Foso District Court, allowing officers to obtain subscriber information from MTN to effect the arrest of the suspects.

items.title: Retired Senior Military officer in court over alleged enlistment fraud
items.description: A retired senior military officer has appeared before the Accra Circuit Court, accused of defrauding a man of GH¢1 million under the pretext of facilitating the recruitment of 200 people into the Ghana Armed Forces. Brigadier General (Rtd) Emmanuel Acheampong Baidoo pleaded not guilty to a charge of defrauding by false pretences. Inspector Morga Dorvi, prosecuting, told the court that the complainant, Captain Abel Nettey, a serving military officer residing in Accra, alleged that the accused received GH¢740,000 and an unregistered Toyota 4Runner valued at GH¢260,000 to facilitate the recruitment exercise. The prosecution said that in 2017, Baidoo allegedly represented to Nettey that, having previously assisted him and served as Director of Manpower of the Ghana Armed Forces, he could facilitate the recruitment of the complainant’s relatives into the military. According to the prosecution, Nettey, believing the representation, introduced 200 interested persons to the accused at Burma Camp for recruitment. The court heard that Baidoo allegedly demanded and received the Toyota 4Runner and GH¢740,000 in cash from Nettey for that purpose. Inspector Dorvi said that after receiving the vehicle and money, Baidoo failed to fulfil the arrangement and travelled outside the country. The prosecution said efforts by Nettey to recover the vehicle and money proved unsuccessful, leading to a complaint to the police on September 7, 2026. The Accra Regional Criminal Investigations Department (CID) later invited Baidoo on September 8, 2026, to assist with the investigation. The prosecution said Baidoo denied the allegation in his initial caution statement. However, after witnesses gave statements, the prosecution said he admitted, in the presence of an independent witness, to receiving the money and vehicle from Nettey to facilitate the recruitment of 200 people. The prosecution said Baidoo failed to fulfil the arrangement. The court recovered the Toyota 4Runner, now bearing registration number GR 3335-24, from Baidoo and returned it to Nettey. The prosecution further said Baidoo had refunded GH¢25,000, leaving an outstanding balance of GH¢715,000. The court granted Baidoo bail in the sum of GH¢600,000, with two sureties, and ordered him to deposit his passport with the court registry.

items.title: Woyome dares critics to prove that he took a bribe or engaged in corruption
items.description: A businessman and contender for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) national vice chairmanship position, Alfred Agbesi Woyome, has challenged anyone in the country to produce evidence that he has taken a bribe or engaged in any corrupt act He says claims that he unlawfully took money from the State do not reflect the facts of his case. Addressing NDC delegates in Accra on Sunday, November 22, 2026, Mr Woyome maintained that he had not wrongfully taken money, insisting that the controversy surrounding him was the result of what he described as a wrongful accusation by “some people. “I won’t mention their names”, he said. He claimed that he was accused of using Austria to “intervene in our internal political affairs. I am not even an Austrian.” “I dare anybody to prove Alfred Agbesi Woyome even took a fuel coupon,” he added. He urged the delegates to consider his record and not be swayed by what he said were allegations and narratives that had been propagated against him over the years. Background to the Woyome judgement debt controversy Mr Woyome was at the centre of a major judgement debt controversy involving the payment of GH¢51.2 million to him in connection with arrangements for the construction of stadia ahead of Ghana’s hosting of the 2008 Africa Cup of Nations. He had claimed the money as compensation for financial engineering services linked to efforts to secure financing for the stadia projects. The payment was made following a court judgment and an out-of-court settlement with the government. However, the payment was subsequently challenged, with the Supreme Court in July 2014 ordering him to refund the GH¢51.2 million after ruling that the underlying agreements were unconstitutional because they had not received parliamentary approval as required under Article 181(5) of the 1992 Constitution. Mr Woyome was also prosecuted on charges of defrauding by false pretence and causing financial loss to the State. On March 12, 2015, the High Court acquitted and discharged him on both charges, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish its case. The acquittal, however, did not overturn the Supreme Court’s separate order requiring him to refund the judgment debt to the State. The controversy has remained a prominent issue in the country’s political discourse, with Mr Woyome repeatedly defending himself against accusations surrounding the payment.

items.title: Keta police arrest two suspects over death of fisherman at Kedzi-Havedzi
items.description: The Police in the Keta Municipality of the Volta Region have picked up two suspects in connection with the death of Clarkson Govor, popularly known as CK Govor, at Kedzi-Havedzi. The 43-year-old fisherman and farmer was found dead near a lagoon in the community on November 18, sending shockwaves through the area. Police at Keta said they interrogated one suspect, while they picked up the other to assist with the investigation. They said investigators arrested one of the two persons on suspicion as they work to establish his link to the incident. The Police disclosed that the main suspect is a fisherman and a fetish priest, although they did not provide further details about his identity. Information available to Ghana News Agency indicates that the deceased had bruises on both legs and a suspected stab wound, but the Police said no blood stains were observed at the scene. Dr Nazeefa Yakubu, a Medical Officer at the Keta Municipal Hospital, who later examined the body, pronounced Mr Govor dead at the facility. Due to the unavailability of space at the Keta Municipal Hospital morgue, the body has been deposited at the Abor Sacred Heart Hospital morgue, pending further investigations and autopsy. The Police also disclosed that the mobile phone of the deceased was taken from him and had not yet been retrieved, and that efforts were underway to trace it. Investigators believe other persons may be linked to the incident and have intensified efforts to identify and arrest the remaining suspects. The Police have appealed to residents of Kedzi-Havedzi and surrounding communities to remain calm and avoid actions that could hamper the investigation. They urged the public to assist the Police with any useful information that could lead to the arrest of the other suspects and the recovery of the deceased’s missing phone.

items.title: Man regains erections, normal urination three weeks after Korle Bu penis reattachment surgery
items.description: A man whose penis was severed in a domestic accident has regained the ability to urinate normally and is experiencing good erections three weeks after surgeons at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital successfully reattached the organ. Consultant Urologist at the hospital, Dr Kenneth Klufio, says the patient is recovering well following the complex surgery, with the medical team hopeful that his condition and sexual function will improve further. The patient sustained the injury after slipping while attempting to stand on a water closet (WC), causing it to break and severely injure his external genitalia. He was initially rushed to the Mamprobi Polyclinic before being referred to Korle Bu, where he was immediately taken to the urology theatre for emergency surgery. Dr Klufio explained that the injury extended through the scrotum and completely severed the penis, damaging the urethra and the erectile tissues responsible for erections. Read Also: Man’s penis reattached at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital after accident He said the injury was particularly serious because it affected all three major structures of the penis, including the two erectile bodies that fill with blood during an erection and the urethra through which urine passes. “The urethra rod through which the urine would flow was cut in two, and then the two rods at the top through which the blood would flow for you to get an erection was also cut in two. This was a very serious injury,” he explained. According to him, the patient could have suffered severe blood loss or life-threatening infections without prompt medical intervention. A multidisciplinary team of urologists, anaesthetists and nurses worked together to reconnect the severed structures and restore their functions. “We came together as a team and were able to bring everything together to allow him to be able to urinate. So the tube that carries the urine was rejoined, and the two tubes that will allow you to get an erection were also connected back,” Dr Klufio said. At a review three weeks after the operation, the medical team confirmed that the surgical wound had healed well, with the patient able to urinate without assistance and experiencing good erections. “We are hoping for him to maintain good function as he goes forward,” Dr Klufio added. Recounting how the accident happened, the patient said he was preparing for lectures when he went to the washroom and attempted to position one leg on the WC. “I intended to use the washroom, the WC… I was trying to let my leg be on the WC… But unfortunately, I used only one leg, and then I realised my WC broke. I saw my testes out, so I shouted to my mom to help me,” he recounted. The patient expressed gratitude to the Korle Bu medical team for the treatment and the support he received during his recovery. He also thanked the hospital for making arrangements to ease the burden of his discharge bill. “I’ll say a very big thank you to Korle Bu for seeing me through the discharge payment thing,” he said. Dr Klufio used the opportunity to highlight the services available at the hospital’s Urology and Nephrology Centre of Excellence, assuring the public that several complex urological conditions, including kidney stones, cancers and erectile dysfunction, can be treated locally. He said patients did not need to travel abroad to access specialised urological care, as such services were available at Korle Bu.

items.title: Family seeks answers following death of woman in Keta
items.description: The family of a 24-year-old woman, Rashida Viera, who died under circumstances surrounding an alleged assault by her boyfriend at Abor-Agbolete in the Keta Municipality of the Volta Region, has called for a thorough police investigation to establish the cause of her death. Ms Modukpey Viera, sister of the deceased, told the Ghana News Agency (GNA) that Rashida left the family’s residence at Agbozume on November 14, 2026, to visit her boyfriend at Abor-Agbolete following an alleged misunderstanding involving another female relative. She said that at about 1600 hours on the same day, she received a telephone call from their father informing her that Rashida had allegedly collapsed and had been taken to the Abor Hospital. According to her, their father received the information by telephone from the boyfriend. Ms Viera said that upon arriving at the hospital, the family was informed by medical personnel that Rashida had been brought in dead. She alleged that the family later received accounts from some eyewitnesses claiming that the deceased had been physically assaulted by her boyfriend before her death. According to her, the eyewitnesses alleged that the suspect subjected Rashida to severe beatings and twisted her neck during the incident. Ms Viera further stated that family members observed marks on the deceased’s body, which they believed could be consistent with the alleged assault. She identified the deceased’s alleged boyfriend, known only as “Scripture,” as the person the family suspected to have been involved in the incident. Ms Viera said the family had received information that the suspect had been arrested by the police at Abor. However, she said when some family members visited the police station to confirm his whereabouts, they could not see him and were only told he had been arrested. The Ghana News Agency could not independently verify the reported arrest or establish the suspect’s current status at the time of filing this report. The body of the deceased has been deposited at the Abor Mortuary, pending an autopsy to determine the cause of death. Ms Viera said the family wanted the police to conduct a comprehensive investigation, interview eyewitnesses and establish the circumstances surrounding Rashida’s death. She said the family was determined to pursue all legal avenues to ensure that anyone found culpable was held accountable under the law. The police is yet to officially communicate details of the incident, including the alleged assault, the reported arrest and the progress of investigations.

items.title: 3 suspects remanded over alleged theft of two-year-old baby at Anloga
items.description: Three suspects identified as Godswill Gologa, aged 19, Emmanuel Tetteh, 24, and Promise Gada, 20, have been remanded into police custody by the Anloga District Magistrate Court for allegedly stealing a two-year-old girl at Anloga in the Volta Region. The court arraigned the suspects on November 11, 2026, on charges of child stealing and abetment of crime, and they remain on remand to allow further investigation into the alleged offences, with the case scheduled to be heard again on December 2. In a police case brief available to the Ghana News Agency, the complainant, Senam Kusitor, a 45-year-old trader and resident of Lashibi, a suburb of Anloga, reported the disappearance of her two-year-old daughter, Nancy Mawunyefia Adzo, on October 28. The complainant said she left the child with relatives at their residence while she went out to sell her goods, but when she returned that evening, she discovered the child was missing. The disappearance of the child prompted a complaint to the police, who subsequently commenced investigations and efforts to locate her. Police investigations reportedly led to a breakthrough on November 3, when officers received intelligence that the missing child had been sighted at a house in Adzido, near Keta, with one of the suspects. The police swiftly moved to the location, where the child was reportedly found in the company of the first suspect, Godswill Gologa. The suspect was subsequently arrested, leading to the discovery of a residence where the child had allegedly been kept for about six days. The police case brief indicated that Emmanuel Tetteh and Promise Gada were also linked to the alleged incident, with Tetteh accused of aiding Gologa in keeping the child while knowing that she was not the biological mother. The three suspects were arrested and taken into police custody, where they were cautioned and detained as investigations continued into the circumstances surrounding the disappearance and recovery of the child. They were later charged with child stealing under Section 93 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), while Tetteh and Gada were also charged with abetment of crime under Section 20 of the same Act. The prosecution told the court that the alleged offence occurred on October 28, while the alleged assistance in keeping the child was said to have occurred between October 28 and November 3, 2026, at Ketasco, a suburb of Keta. After the suspects were arraigned, the court remanded them to police custody and adjourned the case to December 2 for further proceedings.

items.title: Countries push back against COP31 final draft accused of abandoning fossil fuel commitments
items.description: A final draft agreement at the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye, has drawn objections from several countries and negotiating blocs over its failure to explicitly mention fossil fuels, the main driver of human-caused climate change. The European Union, the Marshall Islands and Panama are among those opposing the proposed text, arguing that it falls short of the action required to address rising global temperatures and the worsening impacts of climate change. The dispute has prolonged the COP31 negotiations, which have continued for more than 44 hours beyond their scheduled closing time, making them the longest climate talks to run past their expected deadline. ANTALYA, TURKIYE – NOVEMBER 17: Darragh O’Brien, Ireland’s Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment, representing the rotating Presidency of the Council of the European Union (EU), speaks during a press conference organised by the European Commission as part of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), at the Antalya COP31 Venue in Antalya, Turkiye, on November 17, 2026. The European Commission announced its support for Turkiye’s COP31 Presidency goal of increasing electricity’s share of global final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 (35×35). ( Gökhan Balcı – Anadolu Agency ) Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the European Union, criticised the omission of fossil fuels from the proposed agreement. “It’s unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuels.” The draft, prepared by Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum, co-president of the two-week conference, was released in the early hours of Sunday, leaving delegates about three hours to raise objections or request changes before a final meeting was called. Scenes from the High-level South-South cooperation event (SCALE), attended by UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell, COP31 President Murat Kurum, and COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen. (Photo: © UN Climate Change – Kubilay Ciftci) Climate agreements require consensus among participating countries, making objections from opposing parties a significant obstacle to securing a final deal. Fossil fuels divide countries over climate action The proposed agreement refers to the 2023 Dubai deal, which called for transitioning away from fossil fuels, but does not explicitly mention fossil fuels, oil, coal or a phase-out anywhere in its 10-page text. The omission has revived concerns over whether countries remain committed to implementing the outcome reached at COP28 in Dubai. Alden Meyer, of climate think tank E3G, said fossil fuels had been absent from COP final decisions for more than 25 years until the Dubai agreement introduced language on transitioning away from them. He warned that failing to reaffirm that commitment could undermine progress made at previous negotiations. “It would be a real setback if we come out of here with no signal that we were serious about what we agreed to do three years ago.” Russia, however, has supported leaving explicit references to fossil fuels out of the final agreement, highlighting the divisions among countries over how far the negotiations should go in addressing the production and use of coal, oil and gas. Panama has also threatened to formally object to any final agreement that does not address its demands, including a cap on oil production, recognition that existing warming targets are failing, and increased financing for developing countries to adapt to climate change. Earlier in the week, Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, accused the negotiations of being held hostage by a “petroleum mafia” and called for reforms to the climate process. Carbon capture proposal raises concerns While the draft avoids explicit references to fossil fuels, it proposes a target to support technologies that capture carbon dioxide emissions and store them. The proposal calls for capturing, reusing and storing one billion metric tonnes of carbon, an approach intended to help industries that face difficulties reducing emissions through a switch to renewable energy. Carbon capture and storage involves capturing carbon dioxide from industrial processes or other sources before it enters the atmosphere, transporting it and storing it underground or through other approved methods. However, the technology remains contentious in climate negotiations, with concerns that it could be used to justify continued investment in fossil fuel infrastructure instead of rapidly reducing dependence on coal, oil and gas. Rachel Cleetus, of the Union of Concerned Scientists, said the world could not limit the extent of global warming without a rapid reduction in fossil fuel use. “Fossil fuels are the root cause of climate change, and there is no plausible pathway to limit climate overshoot without rapidly phasing them out.” Electrification target included in the draft The proposed agreement also includes Türkiye’s electrification target, which seeks to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption from approximately 21 per cent currently to 35 per cent by 2035. Achieving the target would require countries to expand the use of electricity in sectors that largely depend on fossil fuels, including transport and industrial production. This could involve replacing petrol and diesel-powered vehicles with electric alternatives and using electricity instead of coal in certain industrial processes. Climate campaigners, however, are demanding that the agreement make clear that the electricity powering this transition must come from renewable sources, including wind and solar. They argue that expanding electricity consumption without decarbonising its generation could undermine the climate benefits of electrification, particularly in countries where power generation remains heavily dependent on coal and gas. Bill Hare, chief executive of Climate Analytics, said electrification alone would not be sufficient to reduce global warming if fossil fuels continued to power electricity generation. “Electrification that runs on coal and gas does not limit warming.”

items.title: UK should only rejoin EU if it innovates on technology, Blair warns
items.description: Former prime minister Sir Tony Blair has said Britain should rejoin the European Union (EU) only if it reforms and allows more technological innovation. Speaking to The Sunday Times , Sir Tony said: “I was painted as saying Britain should just go back and rejoin – I’m not saying that – it’s heavily conditioned.” Sir Tony was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, and told the paper: “I do think Brexit was a real mistake.” But he added the debate was different now than it was in 2016. Referencing the need for technology innovation, he said Europe could and “probably are” moving in the wrong direction. He said: “The problem if we go back and join Europe is that I can’t say that the technology revolution is the single biggest thing, and then if Europe moves in the wrong direction on technology innovation, which they might do and presently probably are doing, that it’s a good idea for Britain to rejoin. That’s what’s changed in this last ten years.” He argued Britain should have an ambition to reform the EU. But he added that we have to be “prepared to walk away from that negotiation” and need to make our own economy and tech sector strong. Prime Minister Andy Burnham this week agreed what he called a “win-win” deal with the EU. The agreement covered British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also announced that the trading bloc and the UK are launching a digital partnership, including areas like artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum technology. The EU and Britain “have enormous potential to innovate together”, she added. PM Andy Burnham met EU chief Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa in Brussels on Friday On artificial intelligence, Sir Tony said that “AI is like fire – it can cook your food and burn your house down”. Sir Tony said the risks of AI are “very considerable” and that tech “can be used for good or bad”. “It’s a new world,” he said. He added other countries are “coming up and rising and there is a dynamism and energy in them” and he fears the UK is “not as dynamic and energetic as we need to be”. Burnham was in Brussels on Friday to finalise the latest stage of the government’s post-Brexit “reset” of relations with the EU – which originally began under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. European Council President António Costa said the EU remains “open to have the closest possible relationship” with the UK. The prime minister added that beyond the deal “we do need to consider what is the right long-term relationship”. He said over the coming months before the next UK-EU summit both sides will “seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process” to look at what those options are. He did not discuss whether the UK could rejoin the EU. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the UK-EU deal “isn’t fair”, and Reform leader Nigel Farage called it a “betrayal of the British people”. Earlier this year, Sir Tony urged PM Andy Burnham to restart negotiations on the possibility of the UK rejoining the EU – but with caveats. Writing in a paper from the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change published in September, the former prime minister wrote: “We should be clear that we want back into a formal relationship with the EU. But it must be a Europe on a credible path to reform.” “This is not about rerunning the debates of 2016 but taking a new approach rooted in the reality of 2026,” he added.

items.title: Paiement électronique : les banques algériennes sommées de déployer 180000 TPE en deux mois
items.description: L’Algérie accélère le déploiement des équipements liés au paiement électronique. En plus de la décision de relever les plafonds de paiement par carte bancaire, le ministre des Finances a ordonné ce dimanche 22 novembre aux banques publiques de déployer 180 000 TPE en deux mois, soit l’équivalent 3000 appareils par jour. « Dans le cadre de la promotion des moyens de paiement scripturaux, je vous instruis de prendre, dès ce jour, toutes les dispositions nécessaires au déploiement de 180 000 terminaux de paiement électronique (TPE) », a ordonné Mohamed Lamine Lebbou dans une instruction adressée ce dimanche aux directeurs des banques, au président de l’Abef et au DG du Trésor public. Ces terminaux devront être installés, activés et opérationnels dans un « délai maximal de deux mois à compter de la date du présent courrier, soit au plus tard le 22 janvier 2027 », a exigé le ministre des Finances. Les banques publiques sommées de mobiliser l’ensemble de leurs agences Pour atteindre cet objectif, Mohamed Lamine Lebbou a demandé aux banques publiques de mobiliser « l'ensemble de leurs réseaux d'agences pour identifier les commerçants et les prestataires de services à équiper, assurer la mise en service des terminaux et accompagner leurs utilisateurs. » Il a chargé l’ABEF de coordonner avec les banques la « répartition de l'objectif global » et l'établissement d'un « calendrier de déploiement par banque et par wilaya. » Pour la Direction générale du Trésor et de la Comptabilité, son rôle est d’assurer le « suivi hebdomadaire de l'opération ». « À cet effet, chaque banque lui transmettra, avec copie à l'ABEF, un état d'avancement précisant, par wilaya, le nombre de TPE mis en service au cours de la semaine et en cumul, les écarts par rapport au calendrier ainsi que les mesures correctives engagées », a-t-il précisé. Mohamed Lamine Lebbou a demandé de « mettre en œuvre, sous la coordination de l'ABEF, un plan de communication commun pour sensibiliser les commerçants, les prestataires de services et le grand public à l'usage des moyens de paiement scripturaux ». Les banques « relaieront cette campagne dans leurs agences et sur leurs canaux de communication afin de promouvoir l'acceptation et l'utilisation du paiement électronique », a-t-il ajouté.
