items.title: Judge approves $7.25bn settlement for Roundup weedkiller cancer claims
items.description: A Missouri judge on Friday approved a $7.25bn (£5.5bn) settlement stemming from lawsuits ⁠alleging that Bayer’s weedkiller Roundup causes cancer. Judge Timothy Boyer said the settlement was “fair, reasonable, and adequate”. Bayer, the German biotech giant, had proposed paying the $7.25bn to definitively resolve a legal battle in the US. The nationwide settlement will be paid to Roundup users who are already sick with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and those who fall ill in the future. The company has already paid roughly $10bn to resolve Roundup-related litigation. The settlements to participants range from $10,000 to $165,000, depending on how frequently they used the product, when they were diagnosed with the cancer and how severe their illness was. “[Friday’s] final approval order delivers guaranteed compensation to Roundup cancer victims who have waited more than a decade for justice,” said Christopher Seeger, a court-appointed counsel for cancer patients in the case. Bayer will make annual payments into a fund for up to 21 years, totalling up to $7.25bn. Some attorneys objected to the settlement funds, arguing they were insufficient, but the judge said he did not want to delay payouts to sick victims. Bayer denies that its Roundup product causes cancer. The settlement comes after the Supreme Court in June ruled in favour of Bayer, overturning a $1.25m settlement for a Missouri man who said Roundup and its ingredient glyphosate was to blame for his non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The court ruled 7-2, saying Bayer cannot be sued in state courts because federal regulations do not mandate a cancer warning label. The company has faced thousands of claims in US state and federal courts from people alleging they developed cancer after using the product. Monsanto developed Roundup in the 1970s. Its active ingredient, glyphosate, was identified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer, a unit of the World Health Organisation, in 2015 as a probable human carcinogen. Bayer and some other regulators, including the US Environmental Protection Agency, have disputed those findings. But the issue has forced the company through years of costly litigation in the US, as juries in several states have awarded billions of dollars to herbicide users.

items.title: Finance inclusive : L’APFI devient IFIC-SA
items.description: Un nouveau cap s’est ouvert ce samedi 21 novembre 2026, pour les actionnaires et acteurs de l’Association pour la Promotion de la Finance Inclusive (APFI). Réunis, à Ouagadougou, la structure de micro finance, sous le leadership de ses actionnaires devient Initiative Financière Inclusive et Crédit (IFIC). Les actionnaires et acteurs ont, à la même occasion, portés leur choix sur Hamadou Bonkoungou, cadre de banque doté d’une expérience de 18 ans, pour être le Président du Conseil d'Administration (PCA). La dynamique de se conformer à la loi La rencontre s’est articulée autour de la lecture des textes devant régir la nouvelle société, l'information de chaque actionnaire sur l'état de son apport au capital, et l'élection du Président du Conseil d'Administration. À cela s’ajoute les questions diverses. Le changement de dénomination, résulte de la loi Nr 001-2025/ALT du 13 février 2025 portant réglementation de la microfinance au Burkina Faso. Cette loi fait obligation aux institutions de microfinance de forme associative de se transformer en société anonyme, ou en société coopérative. C’est dans cette dynamique, que les actions ont opté pour la Société Anonyme (SA). Une vision plus claire pour répondre aux besoins des clients Ainsi, l'APFI devient Initiative Finance Inclusive et Crédit (IFIC) SA avec conseil d'administration. La société à un capital de 200 millions de FCFA. Elle aura pour activités principales la collecte de dépôts, les opérations de prêts et les engagements par signature. Sous réserve des autorisations requises, elle pourra étendre son offre à la fourniture de services de paiement, à l’émission et à la distribution de monnaie électronique, au transfert d’argent, à l’affacturage et au change manuel. Elle a pour ambition de mettre à la disposition des ménages, des petits producteurs, des commerçants et des micro et petites entreprises des services d’épargne, de crédit et de paiement adaptés à leurs besoins >> souligne Hamadou Bonkoungou. Pour lui, a structure connaissait des difficultés et il sera procédé à la relance de ses activités. Elle compte toucher des partenaires dans cette optique, afin d’attendre leur objectif. La finance inclusive, un secteur porteur Un autre objectif, non des moindres, est de toucher toutes les personnes qui n'ont pas accès à la finance classique, en leur offrant des services financiers, tout en leur donnant des crédits. Pour le marché, il y a toujours une marge de manœuvre et nous sommes tous engagé. On est convaincu et nous avons des éléments tangibles qui nous permettent de croire que l’avenir sera meilleur >> rassure le PCA Hamadou Bonkoungou. Les portes ouvertes aux nouveaux actionnaires Côté capital, la dizaine d'actionnaires avec ses 200 millions, a l’ambition d’atteindre 03 milliards de FCFA. Invite est faite aux personnes physiques et morales qui veulent investir dans le domaine de la micro finance, de ne pas hésiter. Le secteur est porteur et on a des éléments de preuve la dessus et nous serons heureux d’accueillir de nouveaux actionnaires au sein du CA >> conclut Hamadou Bonkoungou. Jean Narcisse KOUDOU L’article Finance inclusive : L'APFI devient IFIC-SA est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Conseil des ministres : les décisions de Tebboune sur cinq dossiers
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a présidé ce dimanche 22 novembre une réunion du Conseil des ministres durant laquelle, il a donné des instructions et des orientations sur cinq dossiers. D’abord sur les préparatifs de la Conférence africaine sur les startups, le président a souligné que de « tels événements ne doivent pas être en deçà des résultats obtenus lors de la Foire commerciale intra-africaine » d’Alger de septembre dernier. Conférence africaine sur les startups : les instructions de Tebboune Le chef de l’État a ordonné « d'approfondir davantage » les concertations pour préparer cet événement « crucial » pour l'économie du continent, en y associant le Premier ministre et les ministères des Affaires étrangères et de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, sous la supervision du Directeur de cabinet de la Présidence de la République. Abdelmadjid Tebboune a jugé « impératif de réunir toutes les conditions techniques et professionnelles nécessaires à la réussite de la conférence pour nos frères africains invités ». Cartographie sociale Ensuite, il a abordé le projet de la cartographie sociale nationale et demandé la « poursuite des efforts liés » à son élaboration, en assurant une « coordination totale entre les différents secteurs ». Le chef de l’État a aussi ordonné la mise en place d'un « référentiel algérien en matière de données sociales, à tous les niveaux », au lieu de se « contenter de modèles « prêts à l’emploi » importés de l'étranger ». Ligne ferroviaire minière de l’est : Tebboune satisfait de l’avancée des travaux Le troisième dossier traité lors de cette réunion est la réalisation de la ligne ferroviaire minière reliant Blad El Hadba au port d'Annaba, ainsi que du quai minier lancé dans le cadre de l'extension de cette infrastructure portuaire. Le chef de l’État a salué « l'état d'avancement des travaux de ces deux projets » qui devront être achevés durant le premier trimestre 2027. En outre, le président Tebboune a réitéré ses instructions pour « accélérer le déploiement opérationnel de la Société nationale de dragage portuaire dont il avait précédemment ordonné la création afin qu'elle se substitue aux entreprises étrangères qui assurent ces missions en Algérie depuis des décennies ». Le quatrième point concerne le Plan national d'adaptation aux changements climatiques. Selon le communiqué, le président a salué le travail accompli par la ministre du secteur sur cet « important plan, le qualifiant d'apport précieux aux efforts de l'État en matière de protection de l'environnement face aux changements climatiques ». Deux projets sportifs dans la wilaya de Constantine Enfin, le Conseil des ministres a approuvé le projet de création d'un village olympique à Constantine et la réalisation d'un complexe sportif multidisciplinaire dans cette wilaya. Il a ordonné l'élaboration, dans une phase ultérieure, d'une étude relative à la couverture du stade historique Ben Abdelmalek Ramdane. items.title: Tinubu’s reforms will be difficult to stabilise if he’s not re-elected - Wike
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has warned that President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms could be difficult to sustain if he fails to secure re-election in 2027. Wike said the president needed another term to consolidate the policies introduced by his administration, arguing that Nigeria was beginning to move towards economic recovery and prosperity despite the initial hardship caused by the reforms. The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church in Rumueprikom, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State. He said Tinubu had taken courageous decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which he acknowledged came with difficulties for Nigerians. According to Wike, abandoning the president’s policies before their benefits fully materialise could undermine the progress made so far. “This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” he said. Wike argued that the country was entering a phase where the foundations laid by the administration could begin yielding positive results, stressing the importance of continuity. “He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” the minister said. He also cited improvements in the university system, claiming that strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic activities, had become less frequent under Tinubu. The minister further recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in receiving their payments, saying the president’s decisions had helped address some of the challenges confronting the country. Wike called on Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the president needed votes from Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said. He also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in the administration’s appointments, arguing that Christians had received better representation under Tinubu than in previous governments. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” Wike said. items.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
items.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.” Vanguard News The post ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs. items.title: El maestro Carlos Alcaraz, hasta donde él quiera: ni el isquio ni Zverev pudieron con él
items.description: Ahí se las apaña el prestidigitador, ese joven de pulsaciones cero que cuanto más fea se pone la cosa, cuando Alexander Zverev apunta al reenganche —6-3 para él en el tie-break de la segunda manga—y cuando a la mayoría le entra el canguelo, lo hace así de bien, como los ángeles, como si nada: dos dejadas, en forma de caricias, y todo en su sitio. Él, ya Maestro. 23 años tiene y por fin se acabó la maldición, ese impedimento arrastrado por el tenis español masculino desde el 98, Álex Corretja , sucesor de quien abrió vía, Manolo Orantes en el 76. No pudo lograrlo Rafael Nadal ni tampoco Moyà, Ferrero ni Ferrer, pero lo canta bien alto ahora él, murcianico y campeonissimo : 6-2 y 7-6(7), en 2h 02m. Seguir leyendo BAJADA DRÁSTICA CON EL SAQUE Más allá del elevado nivel ofrecido por Alcaraz, llamó la atención el abrupto descenso con el saque por parte de Zverev, que hasta ahora se había mostrado intratable y, de pronto, perdió el punch . Ni rastro del jugador poderoso de los otros días. Muy frágil. Los cuatro aces que firmó son una cifra muy corta para un sacador como él. De hecho, Alcaraz llegó a siete. En la velada previa, contra Daniil Medvedev, le había endosado 16 al ruso, a quien apenas concedió opción; en las semifinales retuvo el 81% con primeros y un 63% con segundos. Por el contrario, ante el español se quedó en unos registros muy pobres: 54% y un 42% de manera respectiva. Después transmitía a los periodistas que la bajada drástica en ambos porcentajes se debía, en gran medida, a unas molestias en el tobillo derecho. No obstante, también precisó que Alcaraz es uno de los grandes restadores del momento. El murciano leyó bien las direcciones y en la fase ofensiva desbordó con mucha claridad. En concreto, su estadística refleja 28 ganadores, por tan solo 12 del alemán. De Viena a Turín, pasando por París, el vencedor ha enlazado 14 victorias y tres títulos. En total suma 30, por lo que está a cuatro del segundo jugador nacional más laureado, Manolo Orantes (34). Este trofeo significa, además, el cuarto bajo techo. Por otra parte, se convirtió en el tenista más joven en ganar los cuatro majors y el torneo maestro. Lo ha logrado con tan solo 23 años, por los 27 que tenía Federer cuando cerró el círculo (2009), y los 29 de Djokovic (2016) y Agassi (1999).

items.title: ‎APC crisis: Tinubu orders Gov Radda, Masari to settle rift
items.description: ‎–Urges APC leaders to forgive one another, unite ahead of 2027 polls ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Sunday in Lagos underscored the virtue of forgiveness at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. ‎ ‎His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, and former Defence Minister, Alhaji Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ‎ ‎Apparently reacting to reports of a quarrel between Governor Dikko Umar Radda and Masari in Katsina State, President Tinubu urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. ‎ ‎ “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. ‎ ‎He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. ‎ ‎President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎The President thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‎ ‎He thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles. ‎ ‎”People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no five naira in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. ‎ ‎”We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. ‎ ‎The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian Clerics as well as Governors of Lagos, Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo States. ‎ ‎Other dignitaries in attendance included National Security Adviser Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat. ‎ ‎Also present were the Minister of Education, Mr Tunji Alausa; Speaker of Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Dr Nasturah Ashir Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful. ‎ ‎The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible.” ‎ ‎He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. ‎ ‎”The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. ‎ ‎”We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. ‎ ‎He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. ‎ ‎Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the President as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity, and inclusive governance, calling these virtues essential pillars for building a united, peaceful, and prosperous Nigeria. ‎ ‎Former Governor of Jigawa, Badaru Abubakar, said Northerners appreciated President Tinubu’s support for the late former President Muhammadu Buhari in his 2015 and 2019 election victories. ‎ ‎Badaru urged Northern voters to reciprocate the gesture and help the President consolidate the administration’s achievements so far. ‎ ‎The Chairman of the occasion and elder statesman, 94-year-old Alhaji Lateef Femi Okunnu, promised to canvass and vote for the President on January 16, 2027. ‎ ‎He said the President has done a lot to be re-elected. ‎ ‎The elder statesman also emphasised the need to uphold justice, saying that the Tinubu administration is focusing on the economy and infrastructure, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as strengthening the naira and foreign reserves. ‎ ‎In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Alhaji Rafiu Tinubu and Alhaja Iyalode Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the President in his determination to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people. ‎ ‎Rev. Honsu Oluremi, Chairman of Lagos State Government House Chapel, referenced the Bible and urged the people to always pray for leaders’ success. ‎ ‎The Coordinator of the Prayer session and the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla, while reading from the holy Qur’an, asked Allah to grant the President success in his affairs and good health. The post ‎APC crisis: Tinubu orders Gov Radda, Masari to settle rift appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Manifeste d’Antalya : Pour une Afrique maîtresse de ses choix et de son destin (Dr Aliou Gori Diouf)
items.description: La COP31 d’Antalya marque un moment de vérité pour la gouvernance mondiale de l’environnement. Au-delà des négociations et des compromis diplomatiques, elle nous invite à une réflexion fondamentale sur la place de l’Afrique dans la définition des politiques environnementales internationales, mais surtout sur sa capacité à faire respecter ses priorités, ses intérêts et son droit légitime au développement. Depuis plusieurs décennies, notre continent prend pleinement part aux efforts internationaux de lutte contre les changements climatiques, de préservation de la biodiversité et de protection des ressources naturelles. Pourtant, un paradoxe demeure : l’Afrique, qui contribue faiblement aux émissions mondiales de gaz à effet de serre, figure parmi les régions les plus durement affectées par les conséquences du dérèglement climatique. Sécheresses récurrentes, inondations, érosion côtière, désertification et dégradation des terres fragilisent nos économies, nos écosystèmes et les conditions de vie de nos populations. Cette situation appelle une exigence de justice climatique. La solidarité internationale ne peut se limiter à des déclarations de principe. Elle doit se traduire par des engagements financiers prévisibles, accessibles et effectivement mobilisés, des transferts de technologies adaptés et un renforcement durable des capacités institutionnelles et scientifiques des pays africains. L’Afrique ne demande pas un traitement de faveur. Elle réclame la reconnaissance de ses droits, le respect des responsabilités historiques et les moyens nécessaires pour conduire sa propre transition écologique. À cet égard, les enseignements de la COP31 doivent nous conduire à dépasser une diplomatie essentiellement défensive, souvent centrée sur la recherche de compromis, pour construire une véritable diplomatie africaine d’initiative. Il ne s’agit ni de remettre en cause le multilatéralisme ni de s’isoler des dynamiques internationales, mais de faire en sorte que l’Afrique participe pleinement à la définition des règles et des orientations qui engagent son avenir. La transition écologique ne saurait être envisagée comme une nouvelle contrainte imposée aux économies africaines. Elle doit devenir un puissant levier de transformation structurelle, de souveraineté économique, d’innovation et de création d’emplois. Nos ressources naturelles, notre potentiel en énergies renouvelables, notre biodiversité et nos capacités humaines constituent des atouts majeurs qui doivent être mieux valorisés au bénéfice de nos populations. Pour le Sénégal, cette ambition s’inscrit dans la dynamique de transformation portée par la Vision Sénégal 2050, qui place la souveraineté, la durabilité et la valorisation du capital naturel au cœur du projet de développement national. Notre pays entend faire de la transition écologique un pilier de sa transformation économique et sociale, en conciliant protection de l’environnement, sécurité énergétique, développement industriel et amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Il est donc essentiel que les politiques climatiques internationales prennent pleinement en compte les réalités économiques et sociales des pays en développement. Les exigences de réduction des émissions, de transition énergétique et de protection des écosystèmes doivent être accompagnées de mécanismes de financement justes et adaptés. Le recours excessif aux prêts, notamment lorsqu’ils aggravent l’endettement des pays bénéficiaires, ne saurait constituer une réponse durable à une crise dont les responsabilités sont historiquement inégales. Nous devons également porter une attention particulière aux nouvelles règles commerciales et environnementales internationales. Les mécanismes de régulation carbone, les normes de production et les exigences de traçabilité ne doivent pas devenir des obstacles supplémentaires à la compétitivité de nos économies. La transition écologique mondiale doit ouvrir des perspectives aux producteurs africains, favoriser la transformation locale de nos ressources et permettre au continent de capter une part plus importante de la valeur créée. C’est pourquoi je partage la nécessité de procéder à un bilan indépendant, rigoureux et documenté de plus de trente années de négociations environnementales internationales. Une telle démarche, portée par l’Union africaine et la Conférence ministérielle africaine sur l’environnement (AMCEN), permettrait de mesurer les engagements tenus, les financements effectivement mobilisés, les transferts technologiques réalisés, mais également les coûts économiques supportés par nos pays et les opportunités de développement perdues. Ce travail doit déboucher sur une doctrine africaine commune, fondée sur des priorités clairement définies, des lignes rouges partagées et une capacité collective de négociation. L’unité africaine ne doit plus être seulement une convergence de positions diplomatiques ; elle doit devenir un véritable instrument de puissance, soutenu par l’expertise scientifique, juridique, économique et financière du continent. Je voudrais particulièrement insister sur trois exigences fondamentales : la justice climatique, la souveraineté écologique et la création de valeur sur le continent africain. La justice climatique impose le respect du principe des responsabilités communes mais différenciées et des capacités respectives. La souveraineté écologique exige que les États africains conservent la maîtrise de leurs choix de développement, de leurs ressources naturelles et de leurs trajectoires de transition. Enfin, la création de valeur suppose que la protection de notre patrimoine naturel s’accompagne d’investissements productifs, de transferts de compétences, d’innovations technologiques et d’emplois décents pour notre jeunesse. L’Afrique doit ainsi passer du statut de continent vulnérable, trop souvent présenté comme bénéficiaire de l’assistance internationale, à celui de partenaire stratégique incontournable dans la construction des solutions environnementales mondiales. Le Sénégal réaffirme son attachement à la coopération internationale et au multilatéralisme environnemental. Mais cette coopération doit être fondée sur l’équité, la transparence, la responsabilité et la réciprocité. Nous devons pouvoir évaluer la qualité d’un accord non pas seulement à l’aune de son adoption, mais surtout à celle des financements réellement disponibles, des technologies transférées, des écosystèmes restaurés, des emplois créés et des populations effectivement protégées. Antalya doit être le point de départ d’un réveil stratégique africain. Un moment où notre continent décide de mieux évaluer ses acquis, de défendre ses intérêts et de prendre toute sa place dans la redéfinition de la gouvernance mondiale de l’environnement. L’urgence climatique ne nous laisse plus le luxe de l’attentisme. Elle nous impose de conjuguer ambition environnementale et exigence de développement, responsabilité internationale et souveraineté nationale, protection de la planète et prospérité des peuples. Car, au fond, il ne saurait y avoir de transition écologique juste si elle condamne une partie de l’humanité à renoncer à son développement. L’Afrique ne doit plus seulement prendre part aux décisions qui engagent l’avenir de la planète. Elle doit contribuer à les concevoir, à les orienter et à les façonner. L’avenir écologique du monde ne pourra se construire durablement sans une Afrique forte, souveraine et pleinement actrice de son destin. Dr Aliou Gori Diouf, Ministre de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique

items.title: Washington governor calls ICE 'out of control' after Seattle airport arrests
items.description: The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents “out of control” after they arrested two people at Seattle’s main airport on Saturday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown , which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month’s midterms . Video footage widely shared on social media on Saturday showed two people being apprehended by masked men at an airport jet bridge. ICE later confirmed it had detained two people it said had overstayed their visas. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said the agency was “completely and totally out of control”. “Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities,” Ferguson wrote on X. “Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics.” Ferguson said at a news conference that the ICE agents may have broken a state law limiting facial coverings for law enforcement, and that he was looking into how they accessed the jet bridge. The federal immigration agency said its officers “conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa” on Saturday morning. The agency confirmed it had detained a second person whom it said would be charged with assaulting a federal officer, alleging she had thrown hot coffee on an ICE agent. “The individual… was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well,” ICE posted on X. Alaska Airlines, which operated the flight that Mendoza and Mejia tried to board, said on Saturday it was “concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action”. “Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials” but does not “direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity”, the company added. The Port of Seattle, which operates the airport, said: “We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers.” This month, Trump appointed Stephen Miller , architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff. Miller faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

items.title: Borno ADC demands whereabouts of detained supporter
items.description: …Gubio chairman says he ordered his release, denies ADC’s allegations By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Campaign Council in Borno State has demanded the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of one of its supporters, Alhaji Muktari, whom it alleged was arrested and detained in Gubio Local Government Area. However, the Executive Chairman of Gubio Local Government Area, Mali Bulama Mali, has dismissed the allegations, insisting that Muktari had been released and had regained his freedom. The Director of Communications of the ADC Campaign Council in Borno State, Bukar Bukar Petrol, alleged that Muktari was arrested by security operatives following a directive from the local government chairman over his involvement in grassroots mobilisation for the opposition party ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Sunday, Petrol alleged that Muktari was arrested on November 21, 2026, at about 10pm by individuals described as repentant Boko Haram members allegedly acting on the instructions of the council chairman. The party expressed concern that Muktari’s whereabouts were unknown to his family and associates, adding that his wife witnessed the incident. It also alleged that the arrest and detention were carried out outside recognised police procedures, with no confirmation that he was taken to a police station or formally processed by law enforcement authorities. The ADC further accused Mali of allegedly empowering repentant Boko Haram members to operate as unofficial security operatives and political foot soldiers in the council. “The circumstances surrounding the arrest are particularly disturbing. Alhaji Mukhtar is reportedly still being held, while his exact whereabouts remain unknown to the party and his associates. His wife witnessed the incident and can provide an account of the circumstances surrounding his arrest,” the statement said. The party described the alleged development as an abuse of public office and raised concerns about the possible creation of parallel security structures and unlawful deprivation of citizens’ liberty. Consequently, the ADC demanded the immediate and unconditional release of Muktari, disclosure of his whereabouts and an independent investigation into the alleged involvement of the council chairman. It also called for an end to the alleged use of repentant Boko Haram members as unofficial security operatives for intimidation, arrests and detention of citizens. The party maintained that a local government chairman had no constitutional or statutory authority to establish a personal security outfit or delegate police powers to unofficial individuals. “The ADC will not accept the use of public office as an instrument of political intimidation, coercion or unlawful detention,” Petrol said. The party warned that it would escalate the matter to national security, human rights and judicial institutions if the authorities failed to address its concerns. However, reacting to the allegations on Sunday, Mali denied ordering Muktari’s arrest, insisting that the ADC supporter had been released on his intervention. The chairman alleged that Muktari, whom he described as a non-indigene of Gubio from Guzamala Local Government Area, was arrested by security authorities over an incident that allegedly caused trouble in the council, and not by repentant Boko Haram members as claimed by the ADC. He said: “Actually, I was the one who ordered for his release and he, Muktari, has regained his freedom, but I cannot guarantee his safety.” Mali’s response contradicted the ADC’s claim that its supporter remained in detention and that his whereabouts were unknown. The post Borno ADC demands whereabouts of detained supporter appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me - Tinubu urges Lagosians to get PVC
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and ensure they collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 elections, declaring that the state remains central to his political ambition. Tinubu spoke on Sunday at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a prayer gathering organised by his family ahead of the general elections. He urged his supporters to reach out to eligible voters in their neighbourhoods and persuade them to participate in the electoral process, warning against complacency. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock your neighbour’s door. Tell them to go and collect their PVCs,” the President said. He jokingly told those without voter cards at the gathering that they had come for the food, drawing laughter from attendees. Tinubu also urged voters to turn out on the scheduled election days, saying their PVCs would give them the opportunity to determine the country’s political direction. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16 and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” he said. Describing Lagos as particularly important to his political ambition, the President said the state’s voting strength should translate into greater participation at the polls. “To me, Lagos is the big deal,” he declared. Tinubu expressed dissatisfaction with the turnout recorded in previous elections, questioning how a state with millions of registered voters could produce relatively low numbers of votes. “How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? No. That’s failure. Even if you win and say you win, is it a win? No!” he said. He further urged residents not to allow disagreements with political leaders to discourage them from voting, saying they could exercise their franchise and still express their grievances afterwards. Tinubu lost Lagos to Peter Obi of the Labour Party in the 2023 presidential election. Obi secured 575,735 votes against Tinubu’s 573,001, despite Tinubu having governed the state from 1999 to 2007. The post 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me - Tinubu urges Lagosians to get PVC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Les Hommes d’El Fadjr » : la controverse continue, Hadda Hazem bientôt jugée
items.description: L’initiative les « Hommes d’El Fadjr » qui vise à encourager les enfants à accomplir la prière de l’aube dans les mosquées, continue de susciter des réactions en Algérie. La secrétaire générale du PT, Louisa Hanoune, a animé, samedi 21 novembre, un meeting populaire à Oran où elle a exprimé son soutien à la directrice du journal El Fadjr. Elle a appelé les autorités « à clore le dossier des enfants de l’aube et à cesser les poursuites à l’encontre de Hadda Hazem qui a exprimé son opinion au sujet de l’éducation des enfants ». Dans ce même contexte, Louisa Hanoune a commenté le rassemblement organisé par l’égyptienne Hala Samir en marge du Sila 2026, à Alger. « Je trouve illogique qu’aucune autorité n’ait réagi face à la ressortissante égyptienne qui a organisé un rassemblement pour diffuser son idéologie et s’immiscer dans les affaires de notre pays, dans un salon ( Sila 2026 ndlr) en plein rue », a déclaré la SG du PT, devant ses partisans réunis à la salle Mediouni d’Oran. « Est-il possible pour un parti ou un intellectuel algérien d’animer un rassemblement en plein rue à l’étranger ? », s’est-elle interrogée. Pour rappel, la directrice du journal El Fadjr a fustigé, dans un message diffusé sur TikTok, le 13 novembre dernier, l’initiative « les hommes d’El Fadjr ». « Les hommes d’El Fadjr » : Hadda Hazem jugée le 29 novembre Le Conseil des imams d’Algérie a dénoncé dans un communiqué publié le 15 novembre, « des atteintes aux lieux saints que sont les mosquées » et « l’usage du discours de haine à l’encontre d’une large frange de la société qui sont les habitués des mosquées ». Le Conseil des imams a appelé « les autorités judiciaires compétentes à ouvrir une enquête pour mettre la lumière sur ces déclarations et prendre les mesures qui s’imposent ». Le même jour, le député du MSP, Omar Maamer, invite le ministre de la Justice à intervenir dans cette affaire. Le parlementaire s’est référé à l’article 2 de la Constitution algérienne qui dispose que « l’Islam est la religion de l’Etat ». Et deux jours après, Hadda Hazem est convoquée, selon Echourouk, pour comparaître le 29 novembre prochain devant le tribunal de Sidi M’hamed à Alger. Si le PT a soutenu Hadda Hazem, le parti Sawt Echaab a en revanche critiqué les déclarations de la directrice du quotidien El Fadjr. « La charia et la croyance sont une ligne rouge. Pour être franc, je défends la liberté d’opinion mais porter atteinte à la réputation des imams et des mosquées, on ne l’accepte pas (…) », a déclaré, jeudi dernier, le président de Sawt Echaab, Lamine Osmani qui a toutefois estimé que la religion ne devait pas devenir un trend sur les réseaux sociaux. L’article « Les Hommes d’El Fadjr » : la controverse continue, Hadda Hazem bientôt jugée est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
items.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation. On Strategies in Criminal Trials: A Practitioner’s Guide, Kekere-Ekun said the publication would be useful to both experienced practitioners and younger lawyers seeking to strengthen their competence in criminal advocacy. She noted that criminal litigation required not only sound knowledge of substantive law but also a firm grasp of procedure, evidence and the strategic decisions that arose at different stages of a trial. She said: “Experience that is not shared may remain a personal achievement. Experience that is documented and transmitted becomes part of the profession’s collective inheritance.” Earlier, Pinheiro praised the CJN for reforms in the judiciary, particularly the digitisation of the Supreme Court’s operations and the refurbishment of federal courts. Pinheiro said the four books he authored were products of his practical experiences as an insolvency practitioner, criminal prosecutor and arbitrator, rather than theoretical exercises. The SAN, who said he would mark 40 years at the Bar in October 2027, explained that the publications represented lessons accumulated over nearly four decades of legal practice and 20 years as a member of the Inner Bar. items.title: Amputee World Cup: Dr Mohammed Raii delivers 30,000 bonus, promises further $120,000 if Black Challenge win trophy
items.description: Ghanaian entrepreneur Dr Mohammed Raii has fulfilled his promise of US$2,000 to each member of the Black Challenge following their historic qualification for the final of the Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Raii, founder of the Eezzy Group Foundation, has also pledged a further US$8,000 to every player if Ghana beat Morocco to lift the trophy. The Black Challenge secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Türkiye on penalties in the semi-finals, following an intense 1-1 draw after extra time. Raii said he wanted to make his commitment clear before the semi-final to avoid the uncertainty and disagreements that can sometimes follow sporting achievements, particularly over promised bonuses. He also wanted the players to appreciate the significance of their achievement and recognise the sacrifices they had made in representing Ghana. The incentive comes as the Black Challenge prepare for another meeting with Morocco, their opponents in the final of the 2024 African Amputee Football Cup of Nations. The two sides will renew their rivalry on Sunday at San Juan de los Lagos, with Ghana seeking to cap their impressive campaign by winning the world title for the first time. Their rivalry has produced some memorable encounters, including the 2023 African Para Games final in Accra, where Ghana came from behind to beat Morocco 2-1. Mohammed Mubarik scored the equaliser before captain Richard Arthur Opentil netted the winner in extra time to secure gold for the hosts. That victory came between Ghana’s African championship triumphs in 2021 and 2024, further establishing the Black Challenge as one of the continent’s leading amputee football sides. Mubarik has continued to play a decisive role in the team’s World Cup campaign, scoring twice in Ghana’s 2-0 quarter-final victory over Egypt to secure a historic place in the semi-finals. Beyond his support for the Black Challenge, Raii has also demonstrated a commitment to para sports in Ghana. In July, his foundation committed GH¢800,000 towards Team Ghana’s campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. “When the world talks about Ghana, we want it to be associated with excellence,” he said during the presentation, according to the Ghana News Agency. Raii has also called on the government, corporate organisations and sporting institutions to invest more in opportunities for people with disabilities to participate in amputee football and other para sports. He believes a lack of assurance about financial and institutional support continues to discourage some potential athletes from getting involved. For now, however, the focus is on Sunday’s final, where the Black Challenge have an opportunity to turn their historic run into a World Cup triumph — and earn another significant reward in the process.

items.title: Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling
items.description: IBADAN—THE Allied Peoples’ Movement, APM, in Oyo State, yesterday, tackled President Bola Tinubu for purportedly attacking the party during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall, in Ibadan. Tinubu, who was in Ibadan on Saturday, took a swipe at the APM and Governor Seyi Makinde. He said: “We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘palẹmọ’ (Pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going.” However, the APM described the president’s remark as desperate distractions from the mounting realities confronting Nigerians and the glaring failures of governance. The party, in a statement by its Director of Communication/Spokesperson Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, said: “We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation. “In Yoruba political parlance, ‘palẹmọ’ evokes the hurried gathering, packing or clearing away of belongings, sometimes suggestive of preparing to leave or carrying away what one can before departure. “Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself. “The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.” The party also warned that traditional rulers, irrespective of their political affiliations, remain ”fathers to all.” “The APM remains confident that Oyo voters will distinguish between political noise and credible leadership, between borrowed prestige and earned trust, and between the spectacle of power and the substance of governance,” the statement said. The post Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Photos: Gunmen set Plateau secondary school ablaze in Bokkos
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, triggered panic in the community after residents noticed smoke billowing from the school premises shortly after church service. A community member, Daniel Bwehfa Makodeng, who reported the incident to journalists, said the school was set ablaze at about 1pm. “Suspected bandits set the school on fire around 1pm,” he said. He explained that residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering about 30 minutes later that the building was on fire. The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Hon. Amalau Amalau, also confirmed the incident, saying the council had received reports that the school was engulfed in flames. Speaking in a telephone interview, Amalau said the circumstances surrounding the fire and the identities of those responsible had yet to be established. “We only saw the school in flames. We cannot ascertain at the moment who was responsible or whether it was carried out by terrorists,” he said. The chairman confirmed that the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the immediate concern was the destruction of the school building. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Photos: Gunmen set Plateau secondary school ablaze in Bokkos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’allaitement maternel exclusif au Maroc ne dépasse pas 35 % durant les six premiers mois
items.description: L’Association marocaine pour la promotion de la santé a appelé à l’adoption de mesures concrètes afin de garantir les droits des mères allaitantes et d’améliorer les conditions de l’allaitement maternel au Maroc. Elle a averti que les campagnes de sensibilisation, malgré leur importance, ne suffisent pas à elles seules à surmonter les obstacles sociaux, professionnels et sanitaires auxquels les femmes sont confrontées. Dans un communiqué publié dimanche, à l’occasion de la clôture de la 16e campagne nationale de promotion de l’allaitement maternel, organisée par le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale en partenariat avec l’Initiative nationale pour le développement humain (INDH), l’association a indiqué que le taux d’allaitement maternel exclusif durant les six premiers mois ne dépasse pas 35 % au Maroc, selon les dernières données nationales disponibles datant de 2018, contre 27,8 % en 2011. L’association a également précisé que seuls 42,6 % des nouveau-nés marocains sont mis au sein durant la première heure suivant leur naissance. Elle a relevé que le taux mondial d’allaitement maternel exclusif a atteint 48 % en 2024, tandis que l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) et l’UNICEF ambitionnent de porter ce taux à 60 % à l’horizon 2030. L'organisation a souligné que ces chiffres sont issus de l’Enquête nationale sur la population et la santé de la famille de 2018 et ne reflètent pas les résultats de la campagne nationale de 2026. Elle a ainsi appelé à la mise à disposition de données nationales actualisées permettant d'évaluer l'évolution des pratiques d'allaitement maternel et l'efficacité des politiques publiques. L’association a estimé que l’allaitement maternel ne relève pas uniquement d’une décision individuelle de la mère, mais dépend également de ses conditions sociales, économiques, professionnelles et familiales. Elle a expliqué que de nombreuses femmes souhaitent allaiter leurs enfants, mais que les conditions de travail, le manque de soutien et l’insuffisance de l’accompagnement sanitaire peuvent les empêcher de poursuivre cette pratique. Dans ce contexte, l’association a plaidé pour un renforcement de la protection de la maternité sur les lieux de travail, à travers le respect des droits liés à l’allaitement, l’aménagement des horaires et des rotations de travail, ainsi que la création de crèches et d’espaces dédiés à l’allaitement, au tirage et à la conservation du lait maternel au sein des entreprises ou à proximité. Elle a également appelé à harmoniser progressivement la protection juridique de l’allaitement maternel entre les secteurs public et privé, afin de garantir aux mères des droits équivalents. Cette protection devrait s’étendre sur une période de 24 mois et inclure un temps rémunéré consacré à l’allaitement, sans discrimination liée à la nature de l’employeur ou au statut contractuel. L’association a par ailleurs relevé des disparités dans l’accès effectif aux droits liés à l’allaitement entre les travailleuses des secteurs public et privé. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité d’accorder une attention particulière aux femmes travaillant dans le secteur informel ainsi qu’aux mères vivant dans des situations de précarité sociale. Les données sur lesquelles s’est appuyée l’association font également ressortir des disparités régionales concernant la mise au sein des nouveau-nés durant la première heure suivant l’accouchement. Ce taux atteint 77,6 % dans la région de Drâa-Tafilalet, contre seulement 25,2 % dans la région de Souss-Massa. Le même indicateur s'établit à 50,2 % en milieu rural, contre 36,5 % en milieu urbain. Pour l’association, ces écarts nécessitent des études plus approfondies afin d’en comprendre les causes et d’orienter les interventions sanitaires et sociales. Parmi les principales revendications formulées par l’association figurent la formation des professionnels de santé à l’accompagnement effectif des mères, la généralisation des pratiques favorables à l’allaitement maternel dans les maternités et la garantie d’un suivi sanitaire continu, depuis la grossesse jusqu’après la reprise du travail. L’association a également demandé la réalisation d’un recensement national des crèches et des espaces d’allaitement sur les lieux de travail, ainsi que la publication régulière d’indicateurs relatifs à la mise au sein durant la première heure après la naissance, à l’allaitement maternel exclusif pendant les six premiers mois et à sa poursuite jusqu’à l’âge de 12 et 24 mois. Enfin, l’Association marocaine pour la promotion de la santé a rappelé que la responsabilité de promouvoir l’allaitement maternel ne repose pas uniquement sur les mères, mais qu’elle est partagée entre les pouvoirs publics, les établissements de santé, les employeurs, les pères et les familles. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité d’apporter un soutien aux femmes sans exercer de pression psychologique sur elles ni les culpabiliser lorsqu’elles ne peuvent pas allaiter ou sont contraintes d'interrompre l'allaitement. The post L’allaitement maternel exclusif au Maroc ne dépasse pas 35 % durant les six premiers mois appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Fin de la XIIIème AG annuelle d’ARINWA à Conakry : voici le discours de remerciement du DG de l’AGRASC
items.description: Madame la Secrétaire générale du Ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, Monsieur le Président du Conseil d’administration de l’Agence de Gestion et de Recouvrement des Avoirs Saisis et Confisqués (AGRASC), Madame la Secrétaire permanente de l'ARINWA , -Monsieur le Président du Réseau inter-agences de recouvrement des avoirs pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest (ARINWA), -Madame la Conseillère chargée de mission au Ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, -Mesdames et Messieurs les Directeurs généraux et Directeurs nationaux, -Mesdames et Messieurs les Représentants des institutions nationales et internationales, -Mesdames et Messieurs les Délégués des pays membres de l’ARINWA, -Distingués invités, en vos rangs, grades et qualités, -Mesdames et Messieurs, Au terme de ces trois journées d’intenses travaux, d’échanges fructueux et de partage d’expériences, c’est avec un réel sentiment de satisfaction et de profonde gratitude que je prends la parole, au nom de l’Agence de Gestion et de Recouvrement des Avoirs Saisis et Confisqués (AGRASC) de Guinée, pour vous adresser nos sincères remerciements. Tout d’abord, je voudrais exprimer notre profonde reconnaissance à Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi DOUMBOUYA, Président de la République, Chef de l’État , pour son engagement constant en faveur du renforcement de l’État de droit, de la bonne gouvernance et de la lutte contre la criminalité économique et financière. J’adresse également nos respectueux remerciements à Monsieur le Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, pour son accompagnement, ainsi qu’à Monsieur le Garde des Sceaux, Ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, pour son soutien déterminant à l'organisation et à la réussite de cette importante rencontre sous-régionale. Je tiens à remercier tout particulièrement le Président d’ARINWA, les membres du Secrétariat permanent, les délégations des pays membres, les experts ainsi que l’ensemble des partenaires techniques et financiers, dont la présence et les contributions ont donné tout son sens à cette Assemblée générale. Votre participation témoigne de notre volonté commune de renforcer la coopération régionale et de faire en sorte que les produits du crime ne puissent plus échapper à l'action de la justice. Mesdames et Messieurs, Pendant trois jours, Conakry a été un véritable carrefour de dialogue, de réflexion et de coopération autour d'un objectif partagé : priver les criminels des profits de leurs activités illicites et faire du recouvrement des avoirs un instrument efficace de justice et de développement. Au-delà des conclusions de nos travaux, je demeure convaincu que cette rencontre aura permis de consolider les liens de confiance, de fraternité et de solidarité entre nos institutions. Je voudrais également saluer et remercier chaleureusement les membres du comité d’organisation, les équipes de l’AGRASC, les services du protocole, de la sécurité, de l’hôtellerie, les interprètes ainsi que toutes les personnes qui, dans la discrétion et parfois au prix de nombreux sacrifices, ont contribué à la réussite de cet événement. Chers participants, chers frères et sœurs venus des pays amis, La Guinée a été particulièrement honorée de vous accueillir. Nous espérons que votre séjour à Conakry vous aura permis d’apprécier l’hospitalité légendaire du peuple guinéen. Si, malgré tous nos efforts, quelques insuffisances ont été constatées dans l’organisation ou durant votre séjour, je vous prie de bien vouloir nous en excuser. Nous espérons surtout que vous repartirez avec d’excellents souvenirs de notre pays et la conviction que la Guinée demeure pleinement engagée aux côtés de ses partenaires dans la lutte contre la criminalité organisée et le recouvrement des avoirs criminels. Je souhaite à chacune et à chacun d’entre vous un excellent retour dans son pays respectif, auprès de sa famille et de ses collaborateurs. Que l’esprit de Conakry continue de nous inspirer et que la coopération entre nos États sorte davantage renforcée de cette 13ᵉ Assemblée générale annuelle d’ARINWA. Vive la coopération judiciaire internationale ! Vive ARINWA ! Vive la République de Guinée ! Je vous remercie de votre aimable attention.

items.title: Any talks with India on terrorism must be 'evidence-based', says Musadik Malik
items.description: Federal minister Musadik Malik said on Sunday that any dialogue between Pakistan and India on terrorism must be “based on evidence”. Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023. Pakistan has repeatedly offered to hold talks with India to resolve outstanding disputes, including the water issue. In video clips shared by India’s ANI news agency on Sunday, Malik responded to queries from Indian media and stressed that he had repeatedly presented Pakistan’s stance before the reporters. “I am giving you a stable response that whenever discussions take place, they will be based on evidence, and they will certainly happen,” he affirmed, saying if New Delhi wanted a “lasting solution”. “You must also have some issues, [though] our issues are much greater than yours, and we also need a lot of evidence […] Whenever dialogue takes place, it will be based on evidence,” the climate change minister reiterated. Malik said Pakistan had repeatedly stated that evidence relating to terrorism could be presented through both bilateral and multilateral forums. “You may bring evidence; we also have evidence that we want to present,” he added. India’s foreign minister had said in June 2024 that his country wanted to “find a solution to the issue of years-old cross-border terrorism” with Pakistan. However, a military conflict between the neighbours last year has intensified tensions and escalatory rhetoric from India. In May 2025, a four-day confrontation between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked to Pakistan. Islamabad had strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation . In another clip, Malik noted that India had invited a representative from Pakistan to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum , a multilateral event. “I am your guest. You invited me to a specific forum; I am present before you. I answered all those questions you asked about this forum,” the minister said, remarking that he had conveyed the “voice of my heart” to the people across the region through the forum. Malik stated, “You are today asking me questions for which you did not invite me. When you invite me for that question, I will appear. However, you first ought to invite me and say ‘we want to speak bilaterally with you’.” ‘Will speak on IWT when invited to do so’ The minister was also asked about his remarks on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), but said he would comment on the matter when invited to do so. “You have currently invited me to speak on topics about which I have already spoken, that when temperatures rise, climate is destroyed, Glofs happen. Glofs and glaciers are blind, they do not know whether to fall on the right or the left,” he said, highlighting the shared threat climate change poses to both neighbours. He further said, “You have called me for culture and civilisation [discussions]. I am your guest, you are my host […] You have asked me the same question a 100 times and I have responded to it a 100 times.” In his remarks at the SCO forum on Saturday, Malik had termed climate change an “enemy” of civilisations and pointed out its impact on South Asian countries that bore the brunt of climate destruction. Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between Pakistan and India, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year after the Pahalgam attack, which was followed by the four-day military conflict between the two sides. Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that New Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. Backing Islamabad’s stance, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) on Aug 31 ordered New Delhi to uphold the IWT, declaring that the treaty remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement. The IWT, brokered by the World Bank in 1960, allocates the three western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — largely to Pakistan, and the three eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — to India. The treaty has survived wars, crises, and political tensions for more than six decades and is considered a rare example of durable water-sharing cooperation between the two neighbours.

items.title: Subsidy Removal: You can’t wish away Nigerians’ hardship, ADC-PCC tells Tinubu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his insistence that Nigerians should forget fuel subsidy, accusing him of being insensitive to the economic hardship confronting millions of citizens. The Council said the President’s remarks exposed his disconnect from Nigerians struggling with rising food prices, soaring transportation costs, poverty and an increasingly unbearable cost of living. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to Tinubu’s declaration at a rally at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, that fuel subsidy belonged to the country’s past. Ologbondiyan spoke during an interaction with youths in Lokoja, ahead of the Council’s presidential campaign rally in Kogi State. “The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. He has demonstrated little or no concern for the suffering of ordinary Nigerians. “That explains his brash insistence that Nigerians should forget about fuel subsidy removal simply because, in his estimation, it belongs to the past,” he said. Questioning how the consequences of the policy could be dismissed when Nigerians continued to bear its effects, Ologbondiyan asked: “How can hardship, hunger and widespread poverty, which are direct consequences of the hurriedly imposed economic policies of the Tinubu administration, suddenly become things of the past when Nigerians continue to bear their devastating consequences every day?” The Council argued that subsidy removal was announced without adequate preparation, effective safety nets or meaningful measures to cushion its impact on vulnerable citizens. It said the policy had contributed to soaring transportation costs, unaffordable food prices, struggling small businesses and worsening poverty among households. “To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” Ologbondiyan added. The ADC-PCC maintained that responsible leadership required acknowledging policy failures and making necessary adjustments to ease citizens’ hardship, rather than defending policies despite their consequences. Beyond the economic crisis, the Council accused the Tinubu administration of weakening critical democratic institutions, including the judiciary, security agencies, anti-corruption bodies and financial institutions, allegedly to advance the President’s second-term ambition. It warned that institutions established to safeguard democracy and protect the public interest must not be subordinated to the political ambitions of any individual. “Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens,” the Council declared. Describing the country’s economic difficulties as the consequence of poor policy choices, inadequate planning and a failure to prioritise citizens’ welfare, the ADC-PCC insisted that the situation was neither inevitable nor beyond remedy. It endorsed its presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the leader capable of reversing the economic decline, restoring investor confidence and rebuilding democratic institutions. The Council said an Atiku-led administration would pursue properly planned economic policies, effective social protection mechanisms and a more humane approach to governance. It urged Nigerians to use lawful and democratic means to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, arguing that the coming election offered an opportunity to change the country’s direction. “Nigerians deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable. “In 2027, Nigerians will have the opportunity to change this narrative. The power to rescue the country and restore hope rests firmly in their hands,” the ADC-PCC said. items.title: Varma century in vain as Pakistan Shaheens down India A in Asia Cup Rising Stars clash
items.description: Pakistan Shaheens overcame a late challenge from Tilak Varma to beat India A by 48 runs in their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha on Sunday, defending a total of 313 after bowling out their opponents with five balls to spare. Skipper Varma struck a century before becoming the last man dismissed for 100 off 149 balls, while Shahbaz Ahmed made 56 in a seventh-wicket stand that briefly revived India’s hopes. But Pakistan’s bowlers held their nerve in the closing overs, with Hasan Nawaz claiming three wickets and Ali Raza taking three for 56. India’s chase had begun to unravel after an explosive start from Abhishek Sharma. The left-hander made 70 off just 42 balls, hitting six fours and six sixes, but his dismissal at 93-3 in the 16th over left the visitors with considerable ground to make up. Pakistan’s spinners then tightened their grip. Sufyan Moqim bowled Kumar Kushagra for two before Hasan removed Rinku Singh and Suryansh Shedge, leaving India struggling at 129-6 in the 26th over. Varma, who had struggled to find the boundary during the middle overs, found support in Shahbaz. The pair added 112 runs for the seventh wicket, taking the score to 241 before Raza broke the stand by having Shahbaz caught by Hasan for 56 off 49 balls. Raza then bowled Vipraj Nigam for a duck, while Imran Randhawa dismissed Harshit Rana to leave India nine down. Varma reached his second century of the tournament, but the milestone offered little consolation as Ahmed Daniyal had him caught by wicket-keeper Rohail Nazir in the 50th over to seal Pakistan’s victory. Controversial toss Earlier, Pakistan had posted 313 after winning a dramatic toss and electing to bat on a slightly dry surface. The toss decision was initially called incorrectly by the match referee, who announced tails after Varma flipped the coin on Pakistan skipper Abdul Samad’s call of heads. Samad pointed out the error and the officials corrected the decision in Pakistan’s favour. The captains did not shake hands, continuing the protocol observed in recent encounters between the sides. Pakistan’s openers Shamyl Hussain and Maaz Sadaqat gave their side a flying start, putting on 66 for the first wicket. Shamyl made 33 off 23 balls before Ayush Badoni had him caught by Harshit Rana at short third. Rana then trapped Rohail leg-before for a duck, with Pakistan on 67-2. The exchanges between Rana and the Pakistan batters had added an edge to the powerplay, with the Indian fast bowler involved in heated verbal exchanges and giving Shamyl an animated send-off. Maaz and Hasan rebuilt the innings, with the former scoring 59 off 63 balls for his second successive half-century. Hasan went on to make 79 off 82 deliveries, while Farhan Yousaf’s 56 off 48 balls and Imran’s quickfire 23 helped Pakistan push past 300, which was proven enough for the side at the end.

items.title: More than 2,300 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive in Pakistan to mark Guru Nanak's birthday
items.description: LAHORE: Over 2,300 Indian Sikh pilgrims arrived in Pakistan through the Wagah Border on Sunday to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism. The visiting pilgrims were received by Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) Chairman Qamar Zaman, Secretary Nasir Mushtaq, Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee (PSGPC) President and Punjab Minorities Minister Sardar Ramesh Singh Arora, the committee’s secretary general Satwant Kaur and other officials at the Wagah border, where the jatha leaders were presented with bouquets. Indian Sikh pilgrims wave to the camera after arriving in Lahore through the Wagah Border to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, on Nov 22. — White Star According to ETPB spokesperson Amir Hashmi, 2,339 Sikh pilgrims arrived from India here on Sunday to take part in the festivities in Nankana Sahib. The Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi had reportedly issued around 3,100 visas to Indian Sikhs. Special counters were set up at the Wagah Border to facilitate immigration and baggage screening, while Rangers were deployed to ensure security . Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive in Lahore through the Wagah Border to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, on Nov 22. — White Star The ETPB had also established currency exchange facilities at the border, while its teams promptly issued identity cards and bus tickets to the pilgrims to ensure a smooth onward journey, he added. “The pilgrims subsequently left for Nankana Sahib in three separate convoys under tight security to attend the main ceremony on Nov 24 marking Baba Guru Nanak’s birth anniversary at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, his birthplace,” Hashmi said. He added that over 20,000 Sikhs — from Pakistan and across the globe — are expected to take part in the formal festivities, which begin today and continue until Nov 24. Indian Sikh pilgrims gather after arriving in Lahore through the Wagah Border to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, on Nov 22. — White Star Federal Minister for Religious Affairs Sardar Muhammad Yousuf, along with other federal and provincial ministers, will attend the event as special guests. The event participants will perform religious rituals, including Bhog and Akhand Path Sahib , followed by a traditional palanquin procession, known as Nagar Kirtan. Speaking on the occasion, ETPB Chairman Zaman said the board was making every effort to ensure that the visiting pilgrims faced no inconvenience during their stay in Pakistan. He said the Indian Sikh pilgrims would return home with fond memories of love, peace and brotherhood. Indian Sikh pilgrims including a wheelchair-bound woman arrive in Lahore through the Wagah Border to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, on Nov 22. — White Star Minister Arora urged the Indian government to immediately reopen the Kartarpur Corridor, which provides Sikh pilgrims with access to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, one of the holiest sites in Sikhism. India suspended movement through the Kartarpur Corridor in May 2025 amid the four-day conflict between the countries. Kaldeep Singh Gurgaj, a leader of the Akal Takht authority from India, said the Sikh community shared a deep bond of reverence with Pakistan, where its members were always treated with respect and honour. “Our gurdwaras in Pakistan are safe and preserved in their original state,” he said. Parmjeet Singh, a leader of a Delhi Gurdwara Management Committee delegation, said Pakistan held special significance for Sikhs as the land associated with their guru. “Pakistan is the land of our guru, and we love it very much,” he said. Indian Sikh pilgrims arrive in Lahore through the Wagah Border to attend celebrations marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak Dev Ji, on Nov 22. — White Star After attending the main ceremony, the Sikh pilgrims will visit Gurdwara Sacha Sauda in Farooqabad on Nov 25 before proceeding to Hassan Abdal, where they will stay overnight at Gurdwara Panja Sahib. They will travel to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Narowal, on Nov 27. The visiting devotees will then spend Nov 29 and 30 visiting various historic gurdwaras in Lahore before returning to India through the Wagah border by road on Dec 1. Sikh pilgrims frequently visit Pakistan to observe events of religious significance. In June, around 600 Sikhs arrived from India to observe the death anniversary of Guru Arjan Dev Ji, known as Jore Mela; before that, about 2,800 visas were issued to pilgrims to celebrate the Baisakhi festival in April.
